findings.title: Entire grade-integrity chain reads a table no code ever writes - permanently empty USP
findings.evidence: getGradeAlerts queries SystemOpsAlert where `trigger_type: { [Op.like]: 'grade%' }` (superadminController.js:345-349). A full grep of backend/src shows SystemOpsAlert is only ever READ - there is NO `SystemOpsAlert.create` and no seeder anywhere (only refs: superadminController.js:345 findAll, superadminDataController.js:570 findAll, :593 findByPk). Nothing in the app emits a grade-type alert (teacher grade-mod requests do not write here). So the `sa_system_ops_alerts` table has zero `grade%` rows in any real deploy, and /api/grade-alerts/ always returns `{alerts: []}`. SAGradeIntegrity (the Integrity Dashboard, the platform USP), SAGradeReport's stats/chart/top-schools/reasons/recent-logs, and the audit drill-down all consume this empty array, so every one of these pages renders its empty state forever. This is mock-data infrastructure presented as a live integrity console.
findings.impact: The flagship 'Grade Integrity' surface - the stated platform USP - is non-functional: no grade-modification request will ever appear, no anomaly is ever surfaced, the SA can never review/validate/flag a grade change. The feature is dead end-to-end despite looking complete.
findings.suggestedFix: Wire a real source: when a teacher/school-admin submits a grade-modification request (or when the event-sourced grade log records an out-of-band change), write a SystemOpsAlert with trigger_type='grade_modification' (or query the actual grade-change/audit-log tables directly in getGradeAlerts instead of the ops-alert table). Until a real source exists, the nav rows should show an explicit 'not yet collecting data' state rather than an empty list that looks broken.

verdict.reasoning: Verified end-to-end and confirmed real. (1) getGradeAlerts (superadminController.js:343-372) queries SystemOpsAlert where trigger_type LIKE 'grade%' against table sa_system_ops_alerts. (2) A full repo-wide grep for SystemOpsAlert.(create|bulkCreate|upsert|build) and raw INSERT INTO sa_system_ops_alerts returns ZERO writes; the only references are reads (superadminController.js:345 findAll, superadminDataController.js:570 findAll, :593 findByPk). There is no seeders dir and no migration seed inserting grade-type rows. So the table has no 'grade%' rows in any real deploy and the endpoint always returns {alerts: []}. (3) All three SA consumers depend solely on this endpoint: SAGradeIntegrity.js:154 (setAlerts from data.alerts), SAGradeReport.js:239 (drives stats, chart, top-schools, reasons, recent-logs all from alerts), and SANotifications.js:67 (grade-alert notifications from gradeAlerts passed down from SuperadminDashboard.js:470). With an empty array every one renders its empty state forever. The flagship Grade-Integrity USP is dead end-to-end. The finding is real and, if anything, understated: the ACTUAL grade-modification data is fully captured but in a DIFFERENT, populated table — pruh_core_modification_request (ModificationRequest model). Teachers POST /api/teacher/modification-requests/ -> ModificationRequest.create (teacherController.js:1982); parents (parentController.js:777) and students (studentController.js:1294) create objections there too; school admins review via reviewModificationRequest (schoolController.js:2467). The SA integrity console simply reads the wrong, never-written table instead of pruh_core_modification_request, so it is wired to a disconnected mock source while live grade-change data sits unused. Severity critical confirmed: the stated platform USP cannot ever surface a single grade-modification request, anomaly, or review action.
verdict.correction: Accurate but understated. The defect is not merely 'a table no code writes' — the real grade-modification data DOES exist and is actively written, just to a different table the SA console never reads. Teacher/parent/student grade-change requests are persisted to pruh_core_modification_request (ModificationRequest model) via ModificationRequest.create (teacherController.js:1982, parentController.js:777, studentController.js:1294) and reviewed by school admins (schoolController.js:2467). Meanwhile /api/grade-alerts/ reads the unrelated, never-populated sa_system_ops_alerts (SystemOpsAlert) table. Correct fix is to point getGradeAlerts at pruh_core_modification_request (filtered/joined for grade-type requests) instead of SystemOpsAlert, so SAGradeIntegrity, SAGradeReport and SANotifications surface the real, already-captured grade-change activity. Confirmed: no seeders directory and no migration seeds the alerts table either.

findings.title: Controller returns 6 flat fields; cards and audit detail read ~15 nested fields it never sends
findings.evidence: getGradeAlerts maps each row to ONLY `{ id, status, school, student, subject, requester:{name} }` (superadminController.js:362-369). But RequestCard reads req.oldGrade, req.oldScore, req.newGrade, req.newScore (lines 89,94,96), req.urgency (line 53), req.term (line 82), req.reason (line 112), req.requester.initials (line 118) and req.ts (line 123) - none of which the controller emits. SAGradeReport's recentLogs likewise reads a.oldGrade/a.newGrade/a.urgency/a.reason/a.ts (lines 268,283-289). Result: even if a grade row existed, every card would show `—` scores, blank reason, blank requester initials, blank timestamp, and the +pts delta, urgency accent, term, and reasons-donut would all be empty/wrong. The CSV export (SAGradeIntegrity.js:244-261) would emit blank Old/New Grade/Score and Hash Match columns. `subject` is just `bodyText.slice(0,120)` (superadminController.js:367) - the first 120 chars of the alert body rendered under a 'Subject' label.
findings.impact: The request cards, the audit detail comparison, the reasons donut, the CSV/PDF/Excel exports, and the recent-logs table are structurally incapable of showing real grade data even after the source is fixed - the API contract and the UI contract do not agree.
findings.suggestedFix: Define one canonical alert DTO (id, status, urgency, school, student, subject, term, oldGrade, oldScore, newGrade, newScore, reason, requester:{name,initials,role}, ts) and have getGradeAlerts populate every field the cards/detail/exports read; or trim the UI to only the fields the backend can supply. Do not ship a card that reads 9 fields the endpoint never returns.

verdict.reasoning: Verified against actual code. getGradeAlerts (superadminController.js:356-369) maps each SystemOpsAlert row to EXACTLY 6 fields: {id, status, school, student, subject, requester:{name}}. The source model SystemOpsAlert.js has only title/body/severity/trigger_type/status/notes/timestamps columns — no grade-specific data exists to emit, and school/student/subject are regex-parsed/sliced from free-text body. There is exactly one getGradeAlerts function feeding the single GET /api/grade-alerts/ route, and BOTH SAGradeIntegrity and SAGradeReport consume that same endpoint's alerts array (no client-side enrichment). The UI consumers read fields the controller never sends: RequestCard (SAGradeIntegrity.js) reads req.urgency(53), req.term(82), req.oldGrade/oldScore(89), req.newGrade/newScore(94,96), req.reason(112), req.requester.initials(118), req.ts(123); the CSV export(244-261) emits Urgency/Old Grade/New Grade/Old Score/New Score/Reason/Hash Match/Timestamp columns; SAGradeReport reads a.reason(268 reasons-donut), a.ts(281-282), a.oldGrade/newGrade(285-286), a.urgency(247,289) for recent-logs and Excel/PDF export(198-209). I also confirmed the 'audit detail comparison' the finding references is SAGradeAuditDetail.js, which receives the raw alert via onDetail(req) (SAGradeIntegrity.js:325) and reads request.oldGrade/newGrade/oldScore/newScore/ts/reason/requester.initials/ip/device/location/hashMatch/blockNum — none emitted. So the cards, audit detail, reasons donut, recent-logs table, and all three export formats are structurally incapable of showing real grade data. The API contract (6 flat fields) and UI contract (~15 mostly-nested fields) genuinely disagree. Two sub-claims are slightly stale: the hash-mismatch badge was already removed from the card (SAGradeIntegrity.js:66-68 comment) and the Hash-Verified stat removed from the report (248-249), but the CSV still emits a Hash Match column reading the never-present r.hashMatch (257) and isFlag still tests a.hashMatch===false (289). This staleness is cosmetic and does not affect the core finding. High severity is justified: grade integrity is the platform's stated USP and the entire surface cannot render real data given the current contract.
verdict.correction: Mostly accurate. Two refinements: (1) The hash/blockchain badge the auditor cites as read on the card was already removed (SAGradeIntegrity.js:66-68 comment), and the Hash-Verified stat was removed from the report (248-249) — so those specific hashMatch reads are partially mitigated, though the CSV 'Hash Match' column (257) and SAGradeReport isFlag test (289) still reference the never-emitted field. (2) The finding cites the audit-detail reads in SAGradeReport, but the richest broken consumer is actually SAGradeAuditDetail.js, which reads request.oldGrade/newGrade/oldScore/newScore/ts/reason/requester.{initials,ip,device,location}/hashMatch/blockNum from the same raw alert object — all fall back to em-dashes/defaults because the controller emits none of them. Core defect (6 flat emitted vs ~15 consumed; blank scores/reason/urgency/term/ts/initials and broken exports) is fully real and unmitigated.

findings.title: Audit detail renders hardcoded evidence files, fake blockchain ledger, and fabricated actor IP/device/location
findings.backend: n/a (no endpoint - all data is props or hardcoded literals)
findings.evidence: SAGradeAuditDetail takes only the `request` object passed from the list (no fetch). The Digital Evidence section hardcodes two fake files `Exam_Scan.pdf` (2.4 MB) and `Mod_Request.docx` (145 KB) for EVERY record (lines 252-253). Actor IP/device/location come from request.requester which getGradeAlerts never populates, so ActorCard always shows the 'N/A' fallback (lines 89-90) while the 'External' red-flag logic keys off IP prefixes 45./103. (line 100) that can never appear. The Blockchain Ledger block renders request.blockHash/blockNum/prevHash (lines 282-300) which no backend emits, so it always falls to 'Record was not committed to the blockchain' (line 305). Validate (line 333 `onClick={() => setValidated(true)}`) and Flag (line 317 `onClick={() => setFlagged(true)}`) only flip local useState - no API call, nothing persists.
findings.impact: An SA opening any grade-audit record sees fabricated forensic evidence (same two file names every time), a permanently 'not committed to blockchain' warning, and Validate/Flag buttons that appear to act but change nothing on refresh. For the platform's integrity USP this is misleading.
findings.suggestedFix: Either build the backing model (evidence attachments, a real grade-change ledger, persisted validate/flag actions writing to the grade audit log) and fetch the record by id, or gate this whole detail behind the feature being real. The honesty banner (lines 128-134) is good but does not excuse shipping a clickable Validate/Flag that no-ops; disable them or wire them to POST.

findings.title: /api/grade-alerts/ is a shared route, not superadmin-gated
findings.evidence: grade-alerts is registered at routes/superadmin.js:100, BEFORE the superadmin-only sub-router `sa` (created at line 111 with `sa.use(requireRole(['superadmin']))`). It sits under the shared block (after authenticateToken + schoolScope at lines 95-96) alongside /dashboard/ and /profile/. So any authenticated user - including a school_admin holding an impersonation token, or any tenant role - can call /api/grade-alerts/ and read cross-school grade-modification alerts. getGradeAlerts also does NO tenant scoping: it findAll's all grade alerts platform-wide (limit 200) with no school_id filter.
findings.impact: Cross-tenant grade-integrity alert data (student names, schools, change reasons) is readable by non-superadmin roles. Low live impact today only because the table is empty, but it becomes a cross-tenant PII leak the moment the source is wired up.
findings.suggestedFix: Move the grade-alerts route under the `sa` sub-router (after line 112) so requireRole(['superadmin']) applies, or add explicit superadmin + tenant scoping inside getGradeAlerts before the source is populated.

findings.title: SAGradeReport has zero @media rules and a hardcoded 2-column risk grid that breaks on mobile
findings.evidence: SAGradeReport is entirely inline-styled with no @media handling. The Risk Analysis grid is fixed `gridTemplateColumns: '1fr 1fr'` (line 444) with className `sa-gi-risk-grid` - the className implies a CSS override exists, but the file imports no CSS and SAGradesAccumulation.css (the only css read in this bucket) has no `.sa-gi-risk-grid` rule. So on a <=600px screen the donut card and the schools-at-risk card stay side-by-side at half width, squashing the donut and bar labels. The chart wrapper is `height:160` with a 400-wide SVG viewBox (lines 379,387) and the recent-logs table relies on the inline `overflowX:auto` wrapper (line 511) only.
findings.impact: On phones the grade-report risk cards are cramped/overlapping and the donut legend wraps badly, violating the mandatory mobile-responsiveness project rule (<=600px rules, >=44px touch targets).
findings.suggestedFix: Add a stylesheet (or extend an existing SA css) with `@media (max-width:600px){ .sa-gi-risk-grid{ grid-template-columns:1fr; } }` and verify the period toggle / 'View All' buttons meet 44px touch targets. Confirm where `.sa-gi-risk-grid`, `.sa-gi-donut`, `.sa-gi-bar-row`, `.sa-progress-*` are actually defined.

findings.title: SAGradeIntegrity and SAGradeAuditDetail rely on shared sa-gi-* classes with no verified mobile rules
findings.evidence: Neither SAGradeIntegrity.js nor SAGradeAuditDetail.js imports a CSS file; both use sa-gi-* classes (sa-gi-card, sa-gi-compare, sa-gi-state-compare, sa-gi-actor, sa-gi-evidence, sa-gi-ledger) that are not defined in SAGradesAccumulation.css (the only bucket css). SAGradeAuditDetail wraps everything in `maxWidth:760` (line 105) and uses a fixed 2-col evidence grid (sa-gi-evidence). Whether these classes carry @media max-width:600px rules cannot be confirmed from the audited files - they must live in a global SA.css. If those rules are absent, the grade comparison boxes and evidence grid will not stack on mobile.
findings.impact: Potential mobile layout breakage on the integrity dashboard cards and audit detail comparison/evidence grids if the shared sa-gi-* classes lack mobile breakpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Verify SA.css contains @media (max-width:600px) rules for .sa-gi-card, .sa-gi-compare, .sa-gi-state-compare, .sa-gi-evidence, .sa-gi-actor-meta, .sa-gi-ledger; add stacking rules if missing.

findings.title: Grade Reports chart hardcodes mid-term/exam-period x-axis labels and a fixed 'anomaly spike' at day 20
findings.evidence: The modification-frequency chart draws a fixed anomaly marker line and red peak dot at array index 20 unconditionally (lines 399-420: `x1={(20/(chartData.length-1))*400}` and `cy={140 - (chartData[20]/Math.max(...chartData))*130}`), regardless of where real activity is. The x-axis labels are hardcoded 'Week 1 / Week 2 / Mid-Term / Exam Period / Finals' (lines 425-429) even though chartData is a per-day count over 30/90 days, not term phases. The legend advertises an 'Anomaly Spike' that is purely decorative. With sparse real data, chartData[20] may be 0, putting the red 'peak' dot at the top of an empty chart.
findings.impact: The chart implies a detected exam-period anomaly that is not derived from data - misleading on the integrity USP, and the labels do not match the actual 30/90-day daily axis.
findings.suggestedFix: Drop the hardcoded day-20 spike marker and the term-phase x-axis labels; render axis ticks from the real date range and only mark a peak at the actual max-value index (or remove the anomaly decoration until real anomaly detection exists).

findings.title: Entering a school does not switch the console — SA shell keeps rendering after enterSchool() swaps the token
findings.evidence: enterSchool() (SuperadminDashboard.js:879-894) does localStorage.setItem('token', data.token); localStorage.setItem('user', JSON.stringify(data.user)); setEnterSchoolOpen(false); window.dispatchEvent(new Event('storage')). But App.js (App.js:178-194) renders <SuperadminDashboard> with NO key tied to token/user and App registers NO 'storage' listener (only popstate at App.js:97). The Dashboard's auth effect that reads localStorage user runs once on mount keyed on stable callbacks (SuperadminDashboard.js:492-509) and never re-runs. So after the token swap the same Dashboard instance keeps its old superadmin `user` state and keeps rendering the SA shell/nav instead of the impersonated school_admin console. Contrast: UserContext (UserContext.js:22) and SchoolBrandingContext (SchoolBrandingContext.js:124) DO listen to 'storage', so branding/user-context update while the actual dashboard surface does not — an inconsistent half-switched state.
findings.impact: The core SA workflow step 'Enter a school' (impersonation launcher) appears to do nothing: operator picks a school, modal closes, but the page still shows the superadmin menu and superadmin data. The school console only appears after a manual full page reload. Primary impersonation entry point is effectively broken from the shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Have App.js listen for the 'storage' event and re-read localStorage user/token to recompute currentPage, and/or pass a key={token} (or a userVersion counter) to <SuperadminDashboard> so it remounts and its auth effect re-reads the new impersonated user. The exit path (ImpersonationBanner.handleReturn) has the same reliance on the dispatched 'storage' event and needs the same App-level listener to take effect without a reload.

verdict.reasoning: Verified end-to-end against the cited code. enterSchool() (SuperadminDashboard.js:879-894) swaps localStorage token/user, closes the modal, and dispatches a synthetic new Event('storage'). The entire SA shell is driven by the component's local `user` state: navItems selection (lines 963-968 choose SUPERADMIN_NAV_ITEMS vs SCHOOL_ADMIN_NAV_ITEMS by user.role), role labels (994/1056), branding gating (980/992), and the teacher/parent/student early-return portals (650-652). That `user` state is set exactly once by the auth-guard useEffect (lines 492-509) whose deps are all stable useCallbacks [onNavigate, fetchSchools, fetchMySchool, fetchGradeAlerts]; it never re-runs. A grep over SuperadminDashboard.js shows the only 'storage' reference is the dispatch at line 890 — the component registers NO addEventListener('storage') and NO location.reload(). App.js confirms it renders <SuperadminDashboard> (lines 187-193) with NO `key` tied to token/user, registers NO 'storage' or 'ek-sms-auth-changed' listener (only popstate at line 97), and its auth/role effect (101-126) runs once with [] deps; even its dashboardData fetch effect is keyed only on currentPage (which stays 'superadmindashboard'), so it won't refetch. So after the token swap the same Dashboard instance keeps its stale superadmin `user` and keeps rendering the operator menu/data. Contrast confirmed: UserContext.js:22 and SchoolBrandingContext.js:124 BOTH addEventListener('storage'), so branding/user-context update while the dashboard surface does not — the inconsistent half-switched state described. Backend confirmed: superadminController.impersonate (line 247) returns {success, token, user} with role:'school_admin' and the school_id (line 272), so a working remount WOULD show the school_admin console — proving the missing piece is purely the frontend remount/re-read. The synthetic same-tab 'storage' event is also a non-trigger for components that don't explicitly listen on window. The core SA 'Enter a school' impersonation launcher therefore appears to do nothing until a manual full page reload. Real, critical, accurately stated.

findings.title: Global search surfaces 'Enter a School' as a normal page and navigates to a StubPage instead of opening the impersonation modal
findings.evidence: GlobalSearch receives pages=navItems with only review/app-history/version-compare/rejection-audit/grade-audit filtered out (SuperadminDashboard.js:1573); the action item {key:'__enter_school', label:'Enter a School', action:'enter-school'} (line 912) is NOT filtered, so typing 'enter' lists it. onSelect runs goTo(item.key) (line 1575) -> setActivePage('__enter_school'). '__enter_school' is not in HANDLED_PAGES (366-389) and has no render block, so it falls through to <StubPage title={getTitle('__enter_school')} /> (line 1508-1510). getTitle has no mapping (271-360) so the title renders as '__enter School'. The sidebar handles this key specially (line 1034: item.action==='enter-school' ? setEnterSchoolOpen(true) : goTo) but GlobalSearch.onSelect does not, so from search it lands on an 'under development' stub.
findings.impact: Searching for the impersonation launcher dead-ends on a broken '__enter School' under-development placeholder instead of opening the Enter-a-School modal. Confusing dead result in the operator's primary search affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Either exclude items with an `action` from the GlobalSearch `pages` list, or make GlobalSearch onSelect honor item.action the same way the sidebar does (open the enter-school modal for 'enter-school' instead of goTo).

findings.title: Sidebar Notifications badge + header bell dot never reflect unread notifications until the operator first opens the Notifications page
findings.backend: n/a (no unread-count fetch on shell mount)
findings.evidence: unreadNotifCount starts at 0 (SuperadminDashboard.js:456) and is ONLY updated via onUnreadChange={setUnreadNotifCount} passed to <SANotifications> (line 1264), which renders only when activePage==='notifications'. There is no fetch of the unread count when the shell mounts. The sidebar badge uses badge: unreadNotifCount (line 959) and the header dot shows when (pendingCount>0 || unreadNotifCount>0) (line 1098). So on login the Notifications badge is always 0 and the bell dot is driven solely by pendingCount until the user navigates into Notifications once.
findings.impact: Operators get no unread-notification signal in the nav/header until they happen to open the Notifications page, defeating the purpose of the badge/dot. New alerts are invisible at a glance.
findings.suggestedFix: Fetch the unread notification count once on shell mount (and on an interval / after actions) into unreadNotifCount, independent of whether the Notifications page is mounted — mirror how pendingCount/gradeAlerts are fetched at init.

verdict.reasoning: Verified against the actual code. In SuperadminDashboard.js: unreadNotifCount = useState(0) at line 456; grep confirms the ONLY setter call site is onUnreadChange={setUnreadNotifCount} passed to <SANotifications> at line 1264. SANotifications renders only when activePage==='notifications' (line 1259). The shell's mount effect (lines 492-509) fetches schools + grade alerts but never computes/fetches a notification unread count. The sidebar badge uses badge: unreadNotifCount (line 959) with NO fallback, so it is definitively 0 until the page is first opened. The header bell dot shows when (pendingCount>0 || unreadNotifCount>0) (line 1098), so it is driven solely by pendingCount (pending school applications) until Notifications is visited — exactly as the evidence states. SANotifications.js confirms the unread count is derived (buildNotifications, lines 18-130) and only emitted via onUnreadChange after its internal effects run (lines 242-246). Notably the shell already holds schools and gradeAlerts at mount, so it could derive the unread signal without opening the page, but buildNotifications is encapsulated inside SANotifications and never invoked at shell level. Adversarial checks did not refute: there is no other setter, no separate mount fetch, and no unread-count backend endpoint that would have masked this. Net effect: sidebar Notifications badge is always 0 on login; bell dot only reflects pending applications, never unread grade/security notifications, until the operator opens Notifications once. Real UX defect. Medium is appropriate — notifications are client-derived from already-fetched data (no data loss, no security impact), and the fix is small (lift buildNotifications or compute unread at shell mount).

findings.title: Header bell dot lights up for pending school applications, not just notifications
findings.evidence: The notification dot renders when (pendingCount > 0 || unreadNotifCount > 0) (SuperadminDashboard.js:1098). pendingCount is the count of schools awaiting an onboarding decision (line 660), a separate concept from notifications. The bell icon implies 'unread notifications' but will show a dot purely because schools are pending review.
findings.impact: Misleading affordance: the bell shows an unread indicator even when there are zero notifications, just because onboarding has a queue. Operator may click the bell expecting notifications and find none new.
findings.suggestedFix: Drive the bell dot from unreadNotifCount only (once that count is fetched at mount per the finding above); the pending-applications signal already has its own badge on the Onboarding/Applications nav item.

verdict.reasoning:
Refuted. The finding's premise is that pendingCount is "a separate concept from notifications," so the bell dot lights with "zero notifications" and clicking it shows "none new." That is false. The notifications page (SANotifications.js) derives its notification list directly from the schools prop, and every pending school produces a first-class UNREAD notification: SANotifications.js:53-62 pushes a {type:'application', severity:'info', title:'New school application submitted', read:false} entry for each school in the pending state (the same predicate, !is_approved && not-rejected/not-changes-requested, that pendingCount counts at SuperadminDashboard.js:660). So when pendingCount>0 there are genuinely unread notifications, and clicking the bell shows exactly them — not "none new."

Moreover, the pendingCount term in the dot condition (line 1098) is functionally necessary, not a bug. unreadNotifCount (line 456) starts at 0 and is ONLY ever set via SANotifications' onUnreadChange callback (line 1264), and SANotifications is a lazy chunk that mounts only when activePage==='notifications' (lines 1259-1268). Therefore, until the operator first opens the Notifications page in a session, unreadNotifCount is stuck at 0 even when unread notifications exist. The `pendingCount > 0 ||` term is what correctly lights the dot in that common fresh-session case for the most frequent notification type (new applications). Removing it would HIDE the dot when there genuinely are unread application notifications — a worse defect. There is no localStorage persistence of read-state, so on every reload a pending school's notification reverts to unread, keeping the dot truthful. The only divergence is the within-session case where the operator marks the pending-application notification read but hasn't acted on the school yet; that is minor staleness, not the "zero notifications" conflation claimed. The dot is accurate, the affordance is not misleading, and the cited behavior is a sensible workaround. False positive.
verdict.correction: The bell dot does NOT light "even when there are zero notifications." Each pending school is rendered as an unread notification on the Notifications page (SANotifications.js:53-62, read:false), so pendingCount>0 always corresponds to real unread notifications, and clicking the bell surfaces them. The pendingCount term is in fact required because unreadNotifCount stays 0 until the lazy SANotifications page is first mounted (set only via onUnreadChange, SuperadminDashboard.js:1264; page rendered only at activePage==='notifications', lines 1259-1268); without it the dot would wrongly stay dark on a fresh session despite unread application notifications.

findings.title: SuperadminDashboard.css is empty (no rules, no @media) — all shell responsiveness depends entirely on SA.css
findings.evidence: SuperadminDashboard.css contains only two comment lines and zero CSS rules / zero @media blocks (full file is 2 lines). The shell's responsive behavior (off-canvas sidebar at max-width:768px, mobile bottom nav, search-modal width clamps) is actually implemented in SA.css (e.g. SA.css:1807-1821 sidebar transform + .sa-mobile-nav display:flex, :3606 .sa-search-modal max-width clamp, .sasc-bar @media at SASchoolScope.css:139). So the shell IS responsive, but the file named for the dashboard carries none of it — a maintainability/colocated-CSS gap, not a runtime defect.
findings.impact: Low: shell renders responsively because SA.css covers it. Risk is future edits to SuperadminDashboard.css assume it controls the shell when it does not; the empty file is misleading.
findings.suggestedFix: Either remove SuperadminDashboard.css (it is import-only with no rules) or move the shell-layout @media rules from SA.css into it so the file name matches its responsibility.

verdict.reasoning: Independently verified every claim. SuperadminDashboard.css (EK_SMS/src/components/superadmin/SuperadminDashboard.css) is exactly 2 comment lines with zero CSS rules and zero @media blocks. The shell's responsive behavior is genuinely implemented in SA.css: the @media (max-width:768px) block at SA.css:1807-1821 sets .sa-sidebar to fixed + translateX(-100%) off-canvas, .sa-wrap.sidebar-open .sa-sidebar transform to reveal it, .sa-menu-btn display:flex, and .sa-mobile-nav display:flex; the search-modal clamp .sa-search-modal { max-width: calc(100vw - 32px) } is at SA.css:3606. SA.css has 28 @media blocks total. The shell JSX in SuperadminDashboard.js actually uses these classes (sa-overlay L974, sa-menu-btn L1070, sa-mobile-nav L1517) and imports both SA.css and SuperadminDashboard.css. So the named file carries none of the shell responsiveness while SA.css carries all of it. This is a real (file is empty) but correctly low-severity maintainability/colocation issue, not a runtime defect — the shell renders fully responsively. The finding's title, evidence, impact, and severity are all accurate, so no correction is needed.

findings.title: GlobalSearch modal is built with inline styles and relies on a single CSS class for its mobile width clamp
findings.evidence: The GlobalSearch modal panel is styled almost entirely inline (SuperadminDashboard.js:196-200) with only className="sa-search-modal" providing width; the width/clamp comes from SA.css (.sa-search-modal max-width:540px default, clamped to calc(100vw - 32px) at max-width:600px, SA.css:3582/3606). Result rows are buttons with ~9px vertical padding (line 239) giving touch targets under the 44px project minimum on mobile. Functionally the modal does navigate (onSelect -> goTo, line 1575) and closes correctly, so this is quality only.
findings.impact: Low: search rows are slightly short for comfortable touch on phones, and the heavy inline styling makes the modal harder to theme/maintain consistently with the rest of the console.
findings.suggestedFix: Move the modal styling into SA.css classes and bump result-row min-height to >=44px on touch to meet the project touch-target rule.

verdict.reasoning: Verified against the actual code. The GlobalSearch modal panel is styled almost entirely with inline styles (SuperadminDashboard.js lines 193, 196-200) and only className="sa-search-modal" supplies width. SA.css confirms .sa-search-modal { width:100%; max-width:540px } (line 3582), clamped to calc(100vw - 32px) at max-width:600px (line 3606) and calc(100vw - 24px) further down (line 3700) — exactly as cited. Result rows are bare <button> elements with no class and inline padding:'9px 16px' (line 239). I confirmed there is NO minHeight anywhere in SuperadminDashboard.js (grep = no matches), and the WCAG 2.5.5 touch-target block in SA.css (lines 3710-3718) only sets min-height:44px on .sa-btn/.sa-select/.sa-text-input/.sa-search-input — none of which the result buttons carry — so the rows are not floored to 44px. With 9px vertical padding plus a 20px page icon (or 0.875rem text), page-result rows render at roughly 38px tall, under the 44px project/WCAG minimum. Navigation and close are intact (onSelect -> goTo + setSearchOpen(false), line 1575; Escape/backdrop close), so this is genuinely quality-only. Severity low is correct.
verdict.correction: The touch-target shortfall is not uniform across all rows, so the row-height claim is slightly overstated. Page-result rows (20px icon + 9px*2 padding ≈ 38px) fall under 44px, but school-result rows use a 28px avatar (28 + 18 ≈ 46px) and meet the minimum. So the defect applies specifically to page-result rows, not every result row. The structural claims (all-inline styling, single class for width clamp, no min-height on the buttons) are fully accurate.

findings.title: School registration discards SA-managed institution/academic/grading master data and uses hardcoded constants
findings.evidence: Register.js:1389-1393 fetches all three endpoints but the extract callbacks are no-ops: `fetchOne('/api/institution-types/', () => { /* options managed client-side */ })`, same for academic-systems and grading-systems. The dropdowns are instead driven by hardcoded constants — Register.js:291 `DEFAULT_INSTITUTION_TYPES`, :310 `DEFAULT_ACADEMIC_SYSTEMS`, :320 `DEFAULT_GRADING_SYSTEMS` — bound via read-only state with no setter: Register.js:1233 `const [institutionTypes] = useState(DEFAULT_INSTITUTION_TYPES);`, :1239, :1240 (single-element destructure, so the fetch can never replace them). Rendered at :1945, :2261, :2267. The whole point of the SA Master Data CRUD for these taxonomies is to feed the registration form; that wiring is dead.
findings.impact: A super admin adding/editing/removing an Institution Type, Academic System, or Grading System sees their change persist in the catalog but it never appears in (or is removed from) the school self-registration form. The CRUD UI looks functional but has no effect on the canonical onboarding workflow it exists to drive.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the no-op extract callbacks with real setters that map the API rows (filtering on is_active) into the dropdown state, and add the missing state setters (`const [institutionTypes, setInstitutionTypes] = useState(...)`). Fall back to the DEFAULT_* constants only when the API returns an empty list.

verdict.reasoning: Verified every cited line. Register.js:291/310/320 define hardcoded DEFAULT_INSTITUTION_TYPES / DEFAULT_ACADEMIC_SYSTEMS / DEFAULT_GRADING_SYSTEMS. Lines 1233/1239/1240 bind them via single-element useState destructures (no setter), so no fetch can replace them. Lines 1390/1392/1393 fetch /api/institution-types, /api/academic-systems, /api/grading-systems but the extract callbacks are genuine no-ops (`/* options managed client-side */`). The dropdowns render from the hardcoded constants at 1945/2261/2267. The backend confirms the rest: superadmin.js:151-210 expose full SA CRUD (POST/PUT/DELETE/toggle) for all three taxonomies, backed by real InstitutionType/AcademicSystem/GradingSystem tables, and the public GETs (superadmin.js:88/92/93 -> getInstitutionTypes/getAcademicSystems/getGradingSystems, controller lines 1542/2537/2582) return curated rows with is_active. So a SA's catalog edits persist and are served by the API, but registration ignores them entirely. The finding is factually accurate. Two adversarial points moderate severity rather than refute it: (1) it is a deliberate design choice, not an accidental bug — the comments ("API data is not curated", "options managed client-side") and the deliberate contrast with countries/regions (which DO prefer curated backend data, 1391/1412) show the developer knew how to wire it and chose not to; (2) there is a real schema mismatch behind the no-op — the academic/grading dropdowns store stable coded enum values ('Semester','percentage','letter_gpa','gpa_4', etc.) that downstream grading/term logic depends on, while the CRUD only stores a free-text `name` with no coded value, so the data can't be swapped in naively. The impact (SA catalog changes never reach onboarding; the CRUD UI looks functional but doesn't drive the workflow it exists for) is real and correctly described, but it is non-blocking (the form works with a sane built-in list) and not a security/data issue, so high overstates it — medium fits a misleading feature-disconnect with an underlying data-model gap.
verdict.correction: The finding is accurate as stated. One refinement: this is an intentional design decision (explicit code comments, and curated backend data IS wired for countries/regions), not broken code — and the root cause that blocks a trivial fix is a schema mismatch: the SA CRUD persists only a free-text `name`, while the academic-system and grading-system dropdowns must emit stable coded enum values that downstream logic relies on. Fixing the wiring requires the master-data rows to carry a `value`/`code` column (and a curated `is_active`-driven list), not just pointing the existing no-op callbacks at r.types / r.academicsystems / r.gradingsystems.

findings.title: New catalog rows are created is_active=false by default (model default), so they are inactive on creation
findings.evidence: Models default is_active to false: CapacityCategory.js:7, InstitutionType.js:7, SchoolType.js:7, SyllabusType.js:7, ClassSubtype.js:7, SchoolCapacity.js:8 all `is_active: { ... defaultValue: false }`. The create handlers never set is_active — e.g. superadminDataController.js:1557 `InstitutionType.create({ name: ... })`, :1781 CapacityCategory, :1867 SchoolCapacity, :2195 SchoolType, :2263 SyllabusType, :2327 ClassSubtype. Consumers filter on is_active (Register.js:1391/1415/1440 use `.filter(c => c.is_active)`), so a freshly-added type is created inactive and is excluded from any is_active-filtered dropdown until the SA notices and manually toggles it on. (AcademicSystem.js:7, GradingSystem.js:7, LessonPlanType.js:8 correctly default to true — the inconsistency itself is a smell.)
findings.impact: After a super admin clicks Add and sees a success toast, the new institution/school/capacity/syllabus/class-subtype is silently inactive and won't surface to schools until they also hit the toggle. There is no in-form hint that Add ≠ Active for these taxonomies, so rows look added-but-broken.
findings.suggestedFix: Either set `is_active: true` in the create handlers for these taxonomies (matching AcademicSystem/GradingSystem), or change the model defaultValue to true. If inactive-on-create is intentional, surface it in SARefDataManager (the create note + an explicit 'Activate' prompt), and make it consistent across all nine types.

verdict.reasoning:
The code-level defect is confirmed. All six catalog models default is_active to false (InstitutionType.js:7, SchoolType.js:7, SyllabusType.js:7, ClassSubtype.js:7, CapacityCategory.js:7, SchoolCapacity.js:8) and every create handler omits is_active (superadminDataController.js createInstitutionType:1557, createCapacityCategory:1781, createSchoolCapacity:1867, createSchoolType:2195, createSyllabusType:2263, createClassSubtype:2327), so new rows are persisted is_active=false. The inconsistency with AcademicSystem.js:7 / GradingSystem.js:7 / LessonPlanType.js:8 (default true) is also real. In the SA UI (SARefDataManager.js) the new row renders as "Inactive" (line 1321, item.is_active ? 'Active' : 'Inactive') and the "Saving only creates / click Roll Out" note (line 706) is hasHero-gated, so these non-year taxonomies get NO in-form hint that Add != Active. That much of the finding is accurate.

HOWEVER the finding's core evidence and impact are mis-stated/overstated, so I lowered severity from high to low. (1) The cited consumer lines Register.js:1391/1415/1440 do NOT filter these taxonomies — they filter countries/regions/cities. (2) Register.js does not consume the backend institution-types catalog at all: it renders hardcoded DEFAULT_INSTITUTION_TYPES (Register.js:291, 1233, 1945) and the /api/institution-types/ fetch explicitly discards the response ("options managed client-side", Register.js:1390); academic/grading systems are likewise hardcoded defaults. (3) Every GET endpoint returns ALL rows with NO is_active filter (getInstitutionTypes:1544, getSchoolTypes:2182, getSyllabusTypes:2250, getClassSubtypes:2318, getCapacityCategories:1768, getSchoolCapacities:1836), so even the SA manager shows the new inactive row. (4) Grep confirms these six models are referenced only by the SA controller/routes/models index — no other consumer anywhere filters them by is_active. So nothing is "silently broken" or "excluded from is_active-filtered dropdowns," and schools are not blocked. Real impact is a UX/data-hygiene wart: SA adds a type, it shows Inactive, they must toggle it on, with no in-form cue. A genuine inconsistency worth a one-line fix (set is_active:true on create or change the model default), but not a high-severity functional defect.
verdict.correction: The defect is real but its consequences are overstated. New catalog rows are indeed created is_active=false (models default false + create handlers omit the field), inconsistent with the three sibling catalogs that default true, and the SARefDataManager create form for these non-year pages shows no "Add != Active" hint. But the claimed downstream breakage is wrong: the cited Register.js filter lines (1391/1415/1440) apply to countries/regions/cities, not these taxonomies; Register.js uses hardcoded DEFAULT_INSTITUTION_TYPES and discards the /api/institution-types/ response; all GET endpoints return rows unfiltered; and no consumer anywhere filters these six catalogs by is_active. The practical effect is a cosmetic/consistency UX issue (the SA must toggle the new row on), not a functional break that hides types from schools. Severity is low, not high.

findings.title: Catalog create/update handlers have no duplicate-name or non-empty validation (unlike Academic Years)
findings.page: institution-type / school-type / syllabus-type / class-subtype / academic-system / grading-system / capacity-category
findings.backend: createInstitutionType / createSchoolType / createSyllabusType / createClassSubtype / createAcademicSystem / createGradingSystem / createCapacityCategory
findings.evidence: Every taxonomy create only checks truthiness, then inserts: superadminDataController.js:1556 `if (!name) return ...; const row = await InstitutionType.create({ name: String(name).slice(0,100) })`; identical at :2194 (school type), :2262 (syllabus), :2326 (class subtype), :2546 (academic system), :2591 (grading system), :1781 (capacity category). No trim (so a whitespace-only name like ' ' passes `if (!name)`), no case-insensitive duplicate check, no per-table unique constraint in the models. Contrast with validateYearPayload (superadminDataController.js:788-835) which trims, length-caps and de-dupes. updateX handlers (:1571, :2209, :2277, :2336, :2556, :2601) are likewise unvalidated.
findings.impact: Super admin can create duplicate 'Government' school types or blank-named rows, polluting the catalog and the registration dropdowns with ambiguous/empty options. No server-side guardrail.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a shared validator for single-name taxonomies: trim + reject empty, length-cap, and case-insensitive duplicate check excluding self on update; return 400 with fieldErrors so SARefDataManager surfaces it inline (it already handles err.payload.fieldErrors at SARefDataManager.js:429).

verdict.reasoning: Verified all cited code. Every one of the 7 taxonomy create handlers does only a truthiness check then a slice with no trim/no dup check: createInstitutionType (superadminDataController.js:1556), createCapacityCategory (:1780), createSchoolType (:2194), createSyllabusType (:2262), createClassSubtype (:2326), createAcademicSystem (:2546), createGradingSystem (:2591). Because a whitespace-only string like ' ' is truthy, it passes `if (!name)` and gets stored (slice does not trim). The update handlers (:1571, :1795, :2209, :2277, :2336, :2556, :2601) are likewise unvalidated. Confirmed the models declare `name` with `allowNull:false` but NO `unique:true` (InstitutionType.js, SchoolType.js, GradingSystem.js read directly; SyllabusType/ClassSubtype/AcademicSystem/CapacityCategory grep for `unique` returned no matches), and allowNull:false does not reject empty/whitespace values. Confirmed routes/superadmin.js wires these handlers with no validation middleware. Confirmed the contrast: validateYearPayload (:788-835) does trim, length-cap, and case-insensitive de-dup, so the asymmetry the finding describes is exactly right. Impact (duplicate or blank-named catalog rows leaking into registration dropdowns) is accurate. Severity stays medium, not high: the only actor is the trusted superadmin/platform operator and it requires operator error to trigger, with no security/tenant-isolation or mass-corruption angle — it is a data-hygiene/UX guardrail gap, but a genuine one that a sibling feature already guards against.

findings.title: Deleting a Capacity Category that is referenced by School Capacities is not blocked (orphan/FK risk)
findings.evidence: deleteCapacityCategory (superadminDataController.js:1805-1816) does `await row.destroy()` with no check for dependent SchoolCapacity rows that reference it via capacity_category_id. getSchoolCapacities (:1840) then looks up `CapacityCategory.findByPk(r.capacity_category_id)` and on a missing parent returns capacity_category_name=null, which the UI renders as the em-dash placeholder (SARefDataManager displayVal). createSchoolCapacity correctly validates the parent exists (:1864), but nothing protects it from later deletion.
findings.impact: A super admin can delete a capacity category still used by School Capacities, leaving orphaned rows that display a blank category name. The two-tab SASchoolCapacity workflow (define categories first, then amounts) is undermined because step-1 data can vanish out from under step-2.
findings.suggestedFix: In deleteCapacityCategory, count SchoolCapacity rows with that capacity_category_id; if >0 return a 409 (the frontend already understands 409+requiresForce, SARefDataManager.js:477) or a plain 400 explaining it is in use. Optionally add an ON DELETE RESTRICT FK.

verdict.reasoning: Verified every claim against the actual code. deleteCapacityCategory (superadminDataController.js:1805-1816) does `await row.destroy()` with no check for dependent SchoolCapacity rows. getSchoolCapacities (:1840) calls CapacityCategory.findByPk(r.capacity_category_id) and returns capacity_category_name=null when the parent is gone (the inner try/catch swallows errors, so it cannot even crash). SARefDataManager.displayVal (SARefDataManager.js:597-598) returns `item[..._name] || '—'` for select fields, so a null category name renders as the em-dash placeholder — confirmed. createSchoolCapacity (:1864) does validate the parent on create, but nothing protects against later deletion — confirmed. Crucially there is NO FK guard at any layer: the Sequelize models (SchoolCapacity.js / CapacityCategory.js) define capacity_category_id as a bare BIGINT with no `references`, models/index.js only bare-requires both with no association, and the migration (2026-05-18-all-new-tables.sql:499-507) declares only a plain `INDEX idx_schoolcapacity_category` — no `FOREIGN KEY ... ON DELETE RESTRICT`. So the orphan is genuinely producible. This is not a universal no-guard codebase: the sibling SystemAcademicYear archive handler (:983-993) counts dependent SystemTerm rows and returns 409 requiresForce, which is the exact guard pattern missing here — confirming an inconsistency, not a non-issue. Severity medium is right: super-admin-only master data, no crash or hard corruption (read path is defensive), but it silently breaks the documented two-tab define-then-amount workflow and leaves blank-category orphan rows.

findings.title: Public (unauthenticated) catalog GETs return inactive rows; clients must filter client-side
findings.evidence: routes/superadmin.js:87-93 mounts these three GETs publicly before `router.use(authenticateToken)` (:95). The handlers return every row regardless of is_active — getInstitutionTypes (:1544) `InstitutionType.findAll({ order: [...] })` with no where clause; same for getAcademicSystems (:2539) and getGradingSystems (:2584). Every consumer is expected to filter is_active itself (Register.js does this for countries/regions/cities at :1391/1415/1440 but, per the dead-wiring finding above, never even reads these three).
findings.impact: Inactive/retired catalog entries are exposed on a public endpoint and would appear in any consumer that forgets to filter is_active. Combined with the is_active=false-on-create default, the contract is fragile.
findings.suggestedFix: Have the public GET variants return only is_active rows (add `where: { is_active: true }`), or expose a documented `?active=1` param and use it from public consumers; keep the SA-authenticated list returning all rows for management.

verdict.reasoning: Core mechanical claim verified. routes/superadmin.js mounts the three GETs publicly before `router.use(authenticateToken)` (lines 88, 92, 93 public; auth at line 95). The handlers in superadminDataController.js do return every row regardless of is_active: getInstitutionTypes (1544) `InstitutionType.findAll({ order:[['created_at','DESC']] })` no where; getAcademicSystems (2539) and getGradingSystems (2584) identical. Each maps `is_active` into the payload, so any consumer must filter client-side. The dead-wiring cross-reference is also confirmed: Register.js (1390/1392/1393) fetches all three but the extract callbacks are empty (`/* options managed client-side */`) — the responses are discarded and the form uses hardcoded options. Countries/regions/cities ARE consumed and DO filter is_active client-side (1391/1415/1440). So the live frontend never surfaces inactive rows from these three. Confirmed real, keep severity low.
verdict.correction: Two parts of the finding are overstated/mis-stated. (1) The "is_active=false-on-create default" amplifier is true ONLY for InstitutionType (model defaultValue:false). AcademicSystem and GradingSystem default is_active:true (models confirmed), so newly created rows there are active — the "fragile contract" argument applies to 1 of 3, not all 3. (2) The finding implies countries/regions/cities filter server-side; they do not — getCountries/getRegions/getCities also do findAll with no where clause and filtering is client-side, so the contract is uniform across all public catalog GETs, not inconsistent. Also note the SAME handlers serve the authenticated SA reference-data management pages (sa.get at 151/201/206) which legitimately must see inactive rows to toggle them — so the handler returning all rows is correct for that surface; only the unauthenticated public mount is debatable, and even then it exposes only low-sensitivity, non-PII master-data names with no live consumer surfacing them. This is best characterized as informational/hardening (drop the unused public institution-types/academic-systems/grading-systems mounts or add a server-side is_active filter to a separate public-only handler), not a functional data-mismatch bug.

findings.title: Thin wrappers are real screens, not stubs — confirmed (no defect, recorded for coverage)
findings.evidence: SAAcademicSystem.js (20 lines) and SAGradingSystem.js (20 lines) are NOT stubs — each renders <SARefDataManager> with a real endpoint, listKey and field config (SAAcademicSystem.js:9-18 endpoint '/api/academic-systems/' listKey 'academicsystems'; SAGradingSystem.js:9-18 endpoint '/api/grading-systems/' listKey 'gradingsystems'). The nav keys render them directly in SuperadminDashboard.js:1403-1404 (`activePage === 'academic-system' && <SAAcademicSystem />`). SARefDataManager provides full loading/empty/error states (SARefDataManager.js:1243-1254) and responsive CSS (SARefDataManager.css:1020,1075,1148,1176). All nine taxonomies (institution-type, school-type, school-capacity, syllabus-type, class-subtype, academic-system, grading-system, lesson-plan-type + capacity-category) have working CRUD UI wired to matching backend listKeys.
findings.impact: None — this entry documents that the ~20-line files are legitimate thin wrappers and the catalog CRUD surface is genuinely functional, so reviewers do not re-flag them as stubs.
findings.suggestedFix: No change required.

verdict.reasoning:
This "finding" is a documentation/coverage note that explicitly asserts NO defect ("impact: None", title says "no defect, recorded for coverage"). I independently verified every claim and they all hold, so there is nothing to fix — isReal=false.

Verified facts:
- SAAcademicSystem.js (20 lines) and SAGradingSystem.js (20 lines) are genuine thin wrappers, not stubs. Each renders <SARefDataManager> with a real endpoint/listKey/field config: SAAcademicSystem endpoint '/api/academic-systems/' listKey 'academicsystems' (lines 9-18); SAGradingSystem endpoint '/api/grading-systems/' listKey 'gradingsystems' (lines 9-18).
