Conclusion: code matches the finding's description, the catalog CRUD surface is genuinely functional, and the finding itself claims no defect. Nothing in the code is broken, missing, or mis-wired, so isReal=false (it is a verified non-issue / coverage record). Severity kept low per the source entry.

findings.title: Grade-alert notifications read fields the controller never returns (urgency / ts / oldGrade / newGrade)
findings.evidence: buildNotifications reads a.urgency (SANotifications.js:68,69), a.subject/a.oldGrade/a.newGrade (SANotifications.js:72-73), and a.ts (SANotifications.js:80). But getGradeAlerts maps each row to ONLY { id, status, school, student, subject, requester } (superadminController.js:362-369) — there is no urgency, oldGrade, newGrade, or ts field. So every grade notification: (a) title always falls to the generic 'Grade modification alert' (urgency undefined, line 68-70), (b) severity always falls back to 'info' (SEVERITY_MAP[undefined], line 78), (c) body always renders 'unknown subject — ? → ?' because oldGrade/newGrade are undefined (line 73), and (d) timestamp = a.ts = undefined, so `new Date(undefined)` is Invalid Date -> relativeTime() returns 'NaNm ago' (line 186-194/400) and the final sort by timestamp (line 130) is corrupted for every grade row. Note `subject` IS returned but holds the first 120 chars of the alert body (superadminController.js:367), not a school subject, so even the subject text is wrong.
findings.impact: Every grade-alert notification shows a generic 'info' card with a meaningless '? → ?' body and a broken 'NaNm ago' timestamp, and pollutes the sort order of the whole feed. The grade-integrity signal — the platform's stated USP — is effectively unreadable in Notifications.
findings.suggestedFix: Either extend getGradeAlerts to return urgency, old_grade, new_grade and a real timestamp (ts/created_at) on each alert object, or change buildNotifications to consume the fields the controller actually emits (status, student, school, requester.name, and an added timestamp). Add a guard so timestamp is never undefined before relativeTime().

findings.title: Sidebar bell badge stays 0 until the user opens Notifications; unread count never loads globally
findings.evidence: unreadNotifCount is initialised to 0 (SuperadminDashboard.js:456) and is ONLY ever updated via onUnreadChange={setUnreadNotifCount} passed to <SANotifications> (line 1264). SANotifications is lazy and only mounts when activePage==='notifications' (line 1259-1267). The sidebar Notifications row renders badge: unreadNotifCount (line 959), so before the operator ever visits the page the badge shows 0 even when there are genuinely-unread items (pending applications, critical security events). Inside SANotifications the report effect is further gated by `if (notifications.length > 0)` (SANotifications.js:243), so an all-empty mount never even resets it.
findings.impact: The unread badge on the primary nav is useless for at-a-glance monitoring — it only becomes accurate after the operator manually opens the page, which is the opposite of what a notification badge is for.
findings.suggestedFix: Compute the unread count at the shell level from data already loaded globally (schools + gradeAlerts, plus a lightweight security-logs/admin-settings fetch) and seed unreadNotifCount on mount, rather than depending on the lazy page mounting. The header dot already partly compensates by OR-ing pendingCount (line 1098), but the numeric sidebar badge does not.

findings.title: Mark-as-read / Mark-all / Dismiss are session-only — no backend, reset on reload
findings.evidence: markRead (SANotifications.js:250-256), markAllRead (258-261) and dismiss (263-269) mutate only local React state — none call ApiClient. The whole feed is re-derived from props/fetches on every mount via buildNotifications (line 225-228), and read-state is only preserved within the live session by the readSet merge (line 234-239). There is no notifications table / no PATCH endpoint, so after a page refresh every dismissed item reappears and every 'mark read' is forgotten (read-defaults are recomputed from is_approved/status each time, lines 33,42,51,60,83,109).
findings.impact: An operator who triages the queue (reads/dismisses items) sees the entire backlog return on the next login. 'Mark all as read' gives a false sense of a cleared inbox. Dismiss is purely cosmetic.
findings.suggestedFix: Persist read/dismissed state — minimally per-user in localStorage keyed by notification id, or properly via a backend read-receipts endpoint. At least scope the localStorage approach the way SAProfile does (ek-sms-... per user.id) so a shared browser doesn't leak state across operators.

findings.title: No loading state while security-logs / admin-settings fetches are in flight
findings.evidence: The useEffect fires two ApiClient.get calls (SANotifications.js:214,217) with no loading flag. notifications starts as [] (line 229) and filtered.length===0 immediately renders the 'No notifications to show' empty card (line 345-349). So during the brief fetch window — or if schools/gradeAlerts props arrive late — the user sees a definitive 'No notifications' message that then flips to a populated list. Errors are swallowed with empty .catch(() => {}) (lines 216,221) so a failed security-logs/admin-settings call surfaces nothing at all.
findings.impact: Momentary 'No notifications to show' flash that contradicts reality; silent failure of the security/system feeds means an operator can't tell 'genuinely empty' from 'fetch failed'.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an isLoading flag covering the initial fetches and the schools/gradeAlerts props, render a spinner/skeleton instead of the empty-state until resolved, and surface a small error notice if the security-logs or admin-settings fetch rejects rather than silently swallowing it.

findings.title: Forensics page is permanently empty — no code ever creates a ForensicEvent row
findings.evidence: getForensicEvents (superadminDataController.js:494-515) reads `ForensicEvent.findAll(...)`, but a repo-wide search for `ForensicEvent.create` returns ZERO hits — no controller, middleware, or job ever inserts a ForensicEvent. The model exists (models/ForensicEvent.js) and the GET is wired, but the table is never written. SAForensics.js:246-267 maps `data.events`; with an always-empty array the page renders only the empty state (SAForensics.js:335-341 'No forensic incidents recorded') and every stat (Open/High/Resolved/Avg, lines 295-307) is permanently 0/'—'. The security-log drill-through (handleForensic -> initialEvent, SAForensics.js:282-289) can therefore never match a case, so 'View forensic detail' from a security event always lands back on an empty list.
findings.impact: An entire top-level System nav page (Forensics, the forensic drill-down from security events) is dead: it can never show data because nothing in the platform produces forensic events. The forensic drill-through button on every security-log row leads nowhere.
findings.suggestedFix: Either emit ForensicEvent rows from the real signals that warrant them (e.g. grade-lock write attempts, hash-mismatch detections, repeated login failures) at the point they occur, or remove the Forensics nav entry until a producer exists. At minimum, derive forensic cases from existing high/critical SecurityAuditLog rows so the page reflects real data.

findings.title: Change Alerts page is permanently empty — no code ever creates a SystemOpsAlert row
findings.evidence: getSystemAlerts (superadminDataController.js:568-587) reads `SystemOpsAlert.findAll`, and postSystemAlerts only ever UPDATES an existing row (findByPk + set status, lines 593-599). A repo-wide search for `SystemOpsAlert.create` returns ZERO hits — nothing creates these alerts for the documented triggers (grade_lock_attempt, enrollment_change, fee_payment, attendance_anomaly, permission_change defined in SAChangeAlerts.js:5-67). So `data.alerts` is always [], the page shows only the empty state (SAChangeAlerts.js:613-624 'No system alerts yet... will appear automatically when trigger conditions are met') and the acknowledge/resolve POST handlers (lines 481-489) have nothing to act on.
findings.impact: The 'System-Wide Change Alerts' page advertises real-time cross-platform change monitoring but can never display a single alert. Its acknowledge/resolve workflow, channel badges, and filter tabs are unreachable in practice.
findings.suggestedFix: Insert SystemOpsAlert rows at the real trigger sites (grade lock attempts, enrollment status changes, large fee payments, permission changes) so the documented trigger_type taxonomy is actually produced. Until a producer is wired, the empty-state copy overpromises ('will appear automatically').

findings.title: Security log 'Status' column is always blank — backend never returns it and model has no such field
findings.evidence: SASecurityLogs.js renders a 'Status' column (header line 237; cell lines 268-270) and computes `statusColor` from ev.status with cases 'Blocked'/'Flagged'/'Allowed'/'Throttled' (lines 244-248). But getSecurityLogs (superadminDataController.js:140-157) returns only {id,type,severity,actor,ip,action,ts,metadata} — no `status`. The SecurityAuditLog model (models/SecurityAuditLog.js:4-16) has no status column at all. So `ev.status` is always undefined: the Status cell renders empty and the entire statusColor branch is dead code.
findings.impact: Every row in the audit/security log shows an empty Status column, making the table look broken or incomplete. The colour-coded status legend the UI implies never appears.
findings.suggestedFix: Either add a `status`/outcome field to SecurityAuditLog and populate it at write time (auditLog.js), then surface it; or remove the Status column and its dead statusColor logic from SASecurityLogs.js.

findings.title: 'Send Now' broadcast only writes a DB row labelled 'sent' — no email/SMS/push is ever dispatched
findings.evidence: The compose UI presents a primary 'Send Now — {target}' button (SAAlertBroadcast.js:263-268) and a success screen 'Alert Sent!' (lines 167-173). But postBroadcastAlerts (superadminDataController.js:538-565) only does `BroadcastAlert.create({ ... status:'sent', sent_at:new Date() })` plus an audit-log row — it never calls sendEmail/Resend, SMS, or push. No school admin actually receives anything; the row is just persisted with a 'sent' label. The audience/target (All Schools, Region: Western, Admin Staff — SAAlertBroadcast.js:227) is stored as a free-text string and never resolved to recipients.
findings.impact: Super admin believes a platform-wide announcement was delivered to school administrators, but nothing leaves the server. Critical security broadcasts silently reach no one.
findings.suggestedFix: On postBroadcastAlerts, resolve the audience to actual users and dispatch via the existing email path (sendPasswordResetEmail's Resend integration is already imported elsewhere), and/or create per-user in-app notifications. Only mark status:'sent' after dispatch; otherwise label it 'recorded'.

findings.title: Broadcast detail 'Acknowledge & Dismiss' claims it is logged for audit but only flips local state
findings.evidence: In AlertDetail the acknowledgment box states 'Your acknowledgment is logged for system audit and compliance tracking' (SAAlertBroadcast.js:88-90), but the button's onClick is just `() => setAcknowledged(true)` (line 98) — no API call. The copy is also hardcoded 'This is a critical security update' (line 89) for every alert regardless of its actual severity/type. The two secondary buttons ('View Full Audit Log', 'Review School Settings', lines 107-116) are permanently disabled/no-op.
findings.impact: The UI asserts a compliance/audit guarantee it does not honour — acknowledgments vanish on re-render and are never recorded. Misleading for a security console.
findings.suggestedFix: Either wire acknowledge to a real persisted endpoint and remove the 'logged for audit' claim until it is, and make the severity/type copy dynamic from `alert.severity`/`alert.type` instead of hardcoded 'critical security update'.

findings.title: Forensic detail 'Acknowledge & Dismiss' and 'Flag for Review' do not persist; chain-of-custody is illustrative
findings.evidence: In ForensicDetail, 'Acknowledge & Dismiss' onClick is `() => setAcknowledged(true)` (SAForensics.js:229) — local only, never marks the ForensicEvent resolved on the server. 'Flag for Review' (lines 223-225) has no onClick at all (dead button). The Chain of Custody (CHAIN_STEPS, lines 22-28) and the SHA-256 hash comparison are static/derived from metadata; the page itself is honest about this ('Illustrative — not a cryptographic chain' line 187; 'Cryptographic signing... not yet implemented' line 218), so this is lower severity, but the action buttons still imply functionality that does not exist.
findings.impact: Operator cannot actually resolve or flag a forensic case from the detail view; the buttons are decorative.
findings.suggestedFix: Wire Acknowledge to a PATCH that sets ForensicEvent.resolved/resolved_at, and either implement 'Flag for Review' or remove it. (Lower priority while the page has no data — see forensics-never-populated.)

findings.title: System Health 'Recent Activity' card is a hardcoded empty placeholder
findings.evidence: SASystemHealth.js:164-169 renders a 'Recent Activity' card whose body is a fixed string 'No recent system activity recorded.' — it never reads any data and there is no corresponding field in getSystemHealth's response (superadminController.js:432-437 returns only status/uptime/services/resources). It will read 'No recent system activity recorded.' forever, even though SecurityAuditLog rows exist and could populate it.
findings.impact: A card that looks like a live feed is permanently static, adding visual noise and implying a feature that isn't there.
findings.suggestedFix: Either feed the card from the latest few SecurityAuditLog/system events (the data exists via /api/security-logs/) or remove the card. The rest of the page (CPU/mem/heap/network via os.* and process.*, db probe, mail config check) is genuinely real — keep that.

findings.title: System Health uptime counter drifts from the real backend uptime between polls
findings.evidence: getSystemHealth returns the real `process.uptime()` (superadminController.js:434). The frontend seeds uptimeSecs from it (SASystemHealth.js:34) but then runs a purely cosmetic +1/second client timer (lines 51-54) that keeps incrementing independently; it is only re-synced every 30s by the poll (line 46). Comment at line 50 even calls it 'Live counter for aesthetic uptime'. If the backend restarts (uptime resets to ~0) the displayed value will be wrong until the next poll, and a frozen/background tab will overshoot.
findings.impact: Minor: the headline uptime can briefly misrepresent the true server uptime. Cosmetic, but it is presented as an authoritative metric.
findings.suggestedFix: Drive the displayed uptime from `lastChecked` plus the last server uptime value (compute elapsed since fetch) rather than a free-running client counter, so a backend restart is reflected immediately on the next poll.

findings.title: Security counter maps 7-day failed-logins into a field named flagged_ips (vestigial mislabel)
findings.evidence: fetchCounters maps `flagged_ips: data.failed_logins_7d` (SASecurityLogs.js:53) — it stuffs the 7-day failed-login count into a state key called flagged_ips. The corresponding stat card was deleted (comment line 92), so the value is currently unused, but the dead mapping remains and is misleadingly named. getSecurityCounters (superadminDataController.js:179-184) emits no flagged_ips at all.
findings.impact: Vestigial/confusing wiring; harmless today because nothing renders it, but a future edit could surface a 'flagged IPs' number that is really a failed-login count.
findings.suggestedFix: Drop the flagged_ips key from the counters state (line 30) and the mapping (line 53) since no card consumes it, or rename to failed_logins_7d if you intend to show it.

findings.title: Reconsider fires an irreversible state change + email on a single click, no confirmation
findings.evidence: SARejected.js:205-210 the Reconsider button does `onClick={() => onReconsider && onReconsider(school)}`; SARejectionAudit.js:357-363 same. In SuperadminDashboard.js:574-576 `handleReconsider` calls `handleAction(school.id, 'request_changes', 'Reconsidering rejected application')` directly with NO confirm modal. handleAction (SuperadminDashboard.js:530-546) immediately POSTs the action. The backend (superadminController.js:210-224) then sends a `sendSchoolChangeRequestEmail` to every school admin. Compare with reject/approve which go through ConfirmModal/ApproveModal in SAReview.js:197-209. So one stray click on the Rejected card both mutates the school out of the Rejected bucket and emails the school, with no undo.
findings.impact: An accidental click silently un-rejects a school and emails its admins asking them to update their application. There is no confirmation step for a state-changing, email-sending action, unlike every other approval action in the console.
findings.suggestedFix: Route Reconsider through a ConfirmModal (reuse SAReview's pattern) that lets the operator add a note before it POSTs request_changes and sends the email.

findings.title: Reconsider sends a hardcoded internal note as the change-request reason; operator cannot say what to change
findings.evidence: SuperadminDashboard.js:575 hardcodes the note: `handleAction(school.id, 'request_changes', 'Reconsidering rejected application')`. The backend uses that note verbatim: the change-request email body is `note || 'Please review and update your application.'` (superadminController.js:218), so the school receives the literal internal phrase 'Reconsidering rejected application' as guidance, AND `school_changes_requested` audit metadata stores note='Reconsidering rejected application' (superadminController.js:232). The reconsider flow gives the operator no field to tell the school what was wrong, even though the whole point is to return it for fixes.
findings.impact: The school is asked to 'update the application' but gets a meaningless internal string as the reason. The audit log records the same uninformative note. Operators cannot explain what to fix on reconsider.
findings.suggestedFix: Capture a real note in the Reconsider confirm dialog and pass it as the action note so both the email body and the audit metadata carry the operator's guidance.

findings.title: Fraud / Incomplete / Policy filter tabs almost never match because rejection reason is free-text and optional
findings.backend: handleSchoolAction reject branch superadminController.js:151 (rejection_reason = note || 'Rejected by superadmin')
findings.evidence: SARejected.js:47-52 defines tabs Fraud Risk / Incomplete Docs / Policy Violation; SARejected.js:79-81 filters by substring on the free-text reason: `(s.rejection_reason||'').toLowerCase().includes('fraud')`, `.includes('incomplete') || .includes('document')`, `.includes('policy')`. But the reject reason is a free-text OPTIONAL field — SAReview.js:103 placeholder 'Reason for rejection (optional)…', and the backend defaults an empty reason to the literal 'Rejected by superadmin' (superadminController.js:151). There is no structured reason category anywhere. So unless an operator happens to type the exact words fraud/incomplete/document/policy, every category tab shows zero results, and the common default reason matches none of them.
findings.impact: Three of the four filter tabs are effectively dead UI that almost always render an empty list, making the operator think there are no fraud/incomplete/policy rejections when really the reason text just didn't contain those keywords.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce a structured rejection-reason category (select in the reject modal) persisted alongside the free-text note, and filter the tabs on that category instead of substring-matching prose.

findings.title: Rejection audit fabricates a fake event timeline when the live log is empty, presented as the record
findings.evidence: SARejectionAudit.js:144-149 builds `fallbackEvents` that invent steps — 'Super Admin opened the application for manual review' (f-review) and 'Rejection Decision Made' with actor 'Super Admin' — and SARejectionAudit.js:148 sets ALL fallback timestamps to `school.registration_date`, so the fabricated rejection appears to have happened at submission time. Likewise rejectedBy/rejectedTs default to 'Super Admin' / registration_date (SARejectionAudit.js:141-142) when no real event matches. realEvents only match if a security log has `metadata.school_id === school.id` (SARejectionAudit.js:123); any school rejected before security-audit logging existed, or whose log row rolled past the limit=500 window, silently shows this fabricated trail. The 'Reconstructed' badge (line 178) is the only hint, easy to miss.
findings.impact: On the audit screen — the page whose entire job is a trustworthy record — a school with no real audit rows shows invented reviewer actions and a wrong rejection timestamp equal to the submission date. An operator could cite fabricated 'facts' from the audit trail.
findings.suggestedFix: When no real audit events exist, show an explicit empty/unavailable state ('No audit events recorded for this school') instead of synthesizing reviewer steps and a fake rejection time; never present invented actors/timestamps in an audit view.

findings.title: Audit trail can miss the rejection event because security-logs is capped at 500 rows with no school filter
findings.evidence: SARejectionAudit.js:106 fetches `/api/security-logs/?limit=500` then filters client-side by school_id (line 123). getSecurityLogs (superadminDataController.js:135) hard-caps `limit` at `Math.min(parsed, 500)` and orders by ts DESC with no per-school query param. There is no endpoint to fetch a single school's audit events; the component pulls the 500 most-recent platform-wide events and hopes the target school's rejection is among them. On an active platform the school_registration_submitted / school_rejected rows for an older rejected school will fall outside the newest 500 and the timeline silently degrades to the fabricated fallback.
findings.impact: For any school whose audit rows are older than the most recent 500 platform events, the 'Live' audit trail can never load — it always reconstructs. The audit page does not scale and gives no indication the data was truncated.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a scoped backend query (e.g. GET /api/security-logs/?school_id=) that returns all events for one school, and have SARejectionAudit call that instead of fetching+filtering the global 500-row window.

findings.title: Reconsider promises 'return to pending review' but backend sets changes_requested, putting the school in a different state
findings.evidence: SARejectionAudit.js:353 tells the operator 'Reconsider this application and return it to pending review for re-evaluation.' But handleReconsider sends action 'request_changes' (SuperadminDashboard.js:575), and the backend sets `school.changes_requested = true` (superadminController.js:203) in addition to clearing rejection_reason/is_active. So the school is NOT in plain 'pending' — it is in 'changes_requested', which the login gate and deriveApprovalStatus (registrationController.js:30) treat distinctly, and which signals the school must edit/resubmit rather than simply await re-review.
findings.impact: The recovery-action copy mis-describes the resulting state. An operator expecting the school to sit untouched in the pending queue instead pushes it into a 'changes requested' state that asks the school to modify its submission.
findings.suggestedFix: Either change the copy to say 'returns the school for changes/re-submission', or add a true 'reopen as pending' action that clears rejection without setting changes_requested, matching the stated intent.

findings.title: getAllSchools returns every school with admins+users on each render, no pagination or filter
findings.evidence: getAllSchools (superadminController.js:77-84) does `School.findAll` with an include of SchoolAdmin -> User and NO limit/where, then serializes all of them. SARejected (and the badge formula in SuperadminDashboard.js:664) receives the entire `schools` array and filters client-side (`schools.filter(s => !s.is_approved && !s.is_active)`, SARejected.js:59). The whole onboarding/rejected/schools surface depends on this one unbounded query; there is no server-side filter for the rejected bucket and no pagination.
findings.impact: As the platform grows the Rejected page (and its badge count, and Onboarding/Schools) load every school with joined admin+user rows on each fetch, growing payload and DB cost linearly. No way to page through a large rejected archive.
findings.suggestedFix: Add server-side filtering (e.g. ?status=rejected) and pagination to getAllSchools, and have the Rejected page request only the rejected slice rather than the full table.

findings.title: Rejection audit shows the fabricated timeline during the initial load instead of a loading state
findings.evidence: SARejectionAudit.js:140 `isReal = realEvents.length > 0`, and line 157 `timeline = isReal ? [...] : [...fallbackEvents...]`. On first paint `loading` is true and `logs` is still empty, so isReal is false and the component immediately renders the reconstructed fallback timeline and the 'Reconstructed' badge; only the small caption at line 252-254 switches to 'Loading live audit events…'. The body timeline shows fabricated events before the real fetch resolves, then snaps to the real trail.
findings.impact: For a moment every audit view shows fake events and a 'Reconstructed' badge even when real data is about to arrive, which is confusing and undermines trust in the audit page.
findings.suggestedFix: Render a skeleton/spinner for the timeline body while `loading` is true and only choose real-vs-fallback after the fetch settles.

findings.title: SystemAcademicYear model uses status + deleted_at columns that no migration creates — every academic-year query 500s in prod
findings.evidence: models/SystemAcademicYear.js:10-15 declares `status: ENUM('draft','active','closed','archived')` and `deleted_at: DATE`. Every controller fn reads/writes these: getAcademicYears (superadminDataController.js:840 `where = {deleted_at:null}`, :875-876 maps `status`/`deleted_at`), createAcademicYear (:904 `status:'draft'`), deleteAcademicYear (:995-996 sets `deleted_at`+`status='archived'`), toggleAcademicYearStatus (:1027/:1031/:1038 `status`), rolloutAcademicYear (:1071/:1075), restoreAcademicYear (:1205-1206), cloneAcademicYear (:1257), closeAcademicYear (:1295). BUT both schema sources omit these columns: migrations/2026-05-18-all-new-tables.sql:479-487 (`pruh_system_academicyear` has only id,name,start_date,end_date,is_active,created_at,updated_at) and migrations/run-all-tables.js:430-438 (identical). No ALTER TABLE adding `status`/`deleted_at` exists anywhere (grep of *.sql). index.js:154 runs `db.sync({ alter: process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' })` — so in production the schema is NOT auto-altered. Because Sequelize findAll selects all model attributes, even the page-load `getAcademicYears` issues `SELECT ... status, deleted_at ...` -> MySQL ER_BAD_FIELD_ERROR -> caught at :884-886 -> 500 `Internal server error`.
findings.impact: In production the entire Academic Years page fails to load (list GET 500s), the SACreateTerm year dropdown shows 'Could not load academic years', and every lifecycle action (create/archive/toggle/rollout/restore/clone/close) 500s. The year+term subsystem is completely non-functional in prod until a manual ALTER runs.
findings.suggestedFix: Ship a migration: `ALTER TABLE pruh_system_academicyear ADD COLUMN status ENUM('draft','active','closed','archived') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft', ADD COLUMN deleted_at DATETIME NULL;` Add it to migrations/run-all-tables.js (and a dated .sql) so prod deploy applies it, and backfill existing rows (status='active' where is_active=1 else 'draft').

verdict.reasoning: Verified against source. models/SystemAcademicYear.js:10-15 declares `status` ENUM('draft','active','closed','archived') NOT NULL and `deleted_at` DATE, with `timestamps:false` (so these are plain selectable attributes, no paranoid/soft-delete magic). The model has NO defaultScope/paranoid that would exclude them, so every findAll/findByPk SELECTs them. Both schema sources omit both columns: migrations/2026-05-18-all-new-tables.sql:479-487 and migrations/run-all-tables.js:430-438 each create pruh_system_academicyear with only id,name,start_date,end_date,is_active,created_at,updated_at. Grep of all four migration files (.sql) found NO ALTER adding status/deleted_at to this table — the one `ADD COLUMN ... status` at line 658 targets pruh_core_teacher, not academicyear. Controller usage confirmed: getAcademicYears builds `where:{deleted_at:null}` (line 840) and maps r.status/r.deleted_at (875-876); createAcademicYear writes status:'draft' (904); deleteAcademicYear sets deleted_at+status='archived' (995-996); toggle (1027/1031/1038), rollout (1071/1075), restore (1205-1206), clone (1257), close (1295) all read/write these columns. index.js:154 runs db.sync({ alter: process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' }) so in prod alter=false and the schema is NOT auto-patched; package.json `start` is plain `node src/index.js` with no migration step, so columns are only added by a manual ALTER (which the project memory itself records as still-pending). Therefore in prod the WHERE deleted_at=null and the implicit SELECT of status/deleted_at hit ER_BAD_FIELD_ERROR, caught at 884-886 -> 500, breaking the list load and every lifecycle action. In dev, alter:true masks it by auto-adding the columns, which is exactly why it reaches prod. Routes confirmed wired (superadmin.js:133-144). One refinement to the finding's impact: school.js:199-200 also routes getAcademicYears/createAcademicYear to the tenant side, so the failure is not limited to the Super Admin surface — tenant school-admin academic-year reads break too, if anything raising severity. Caveat (why not lower than high): I could not inspect the live prod DB or a prod NODE_ENV config file in-repo, so the prod-only failure is contingent on NODE_ENV=production being set and the manual ALTER never having run; but the code path is unambiguous and corroborated by the project's own pending-migration note. Critical severity stands: the entire year+term subsystem is non-functional in prod until the manual ALTER runs.

findings.title: System-term edit / delete / toggle endpoints have NO UI — terms can be created and rolled out but never modified or removed
findings.evidence: SACreateTerm.js only calls POST /api/system-terms/ (create, :238) and POST /api/system-terms/:id/rollout/ (:184, :241). A grep across EK_SMS/src for system-terms shows only those two rollout calls and the create — no apiPut/apiDelete/toggle to system-terms anywhere. The existing-terms list (SACreateTerm.js:359-386) renders each term with only a 'Roll Out' button / 'Active' badge; there is no edit, rename, date-fix, deactivate, or delete control. The three backend handlers (updateSystemTerm, deleteSystemTerm, toggleSystemTermStatus) are wired in routes (superadmin.js:147-149) but unreachable.
findings.impact: A superadmin who fat-fingers a term name/date, or creates a wrong/duplicate term, has no way to fix or remove it from the console. Terms accumulate with no lifecycle management. Three implemented endpoints are dead weight.
findings.suggestedFix: Add edit (inline form), deactivate (toggle), and delete controls to each row in SACreateTerm.js's existing-terms list, wiring to PUT/DELETE/PATCH /api/system-terms/:id/. Mirror the SARefDataManager row-action pattern.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all claims directly. FRONTEND (EK_SMS/src/components/superadmin/SACreateTerm.js, the sole component for the academic-terms page): it only ever touches system-terms via GET list (lines 145, 189), POST create (line 238), and POST rollout (lines 184, 241). The existing-terms list (lines 359-386) renders each term with ONLY a 'Roll Out' button or an 'Active' badge plus name/dates — no edit, rename, date-fix, deactivate, or delete control. A grep for 'system-terms' across the entire EK_SMS/src tree returns exactly one file (SACreateTerm.js), and there is no apiPut/apiDelete/PATCH-toggle call to system-terms anywhere, so no alternate UI surface exists. BACKEND: updateSystemTerm (superadminDataController.js:1464), deleteSystemTerm (:1487), and toggleSystemTermStatus (:1500) are all implemented and wired in routes at superadmin.js:147 (PUT /system-terms/:id/), :148 (DELETE /system-terms/:id/), :149 (PATCH /system-terms/:id/toggle/). They are reachable by API but have zero frontend caller — confirmed dead from the console. SuperadminDashboard.js confirms academic-terms renders only <SACreateTerm/>, so there is no separate 'manage terms' page hosting these controls. The finding is accurate as stated. Severity adjusted high->medium: this is a real lifecycle/management gap (no in-console way to fix a fat-fingered term name/date, remove a duplicate, or deactivate the wrong active term; three endpoints are dead weight), but it is a missing-management-feature, not a security/data-integrity/broken-core-flow defect. The core create+rollout flow works, and on an operator-only single-superadmin surface a mistake can be partially worked around by creating a corrected term and rolling it out. The inability to delete/deactivate means cruft accumulates and a wrongly-active term can't be cleanly removed, which keeps it at solid medium.
verdict.correction: Finding is accurate; only the severity is overstated. It should be medium, not high — the three endpoints exist and are routed (superadmin.js:147-149) but have no UI caller, and the core create/rollout flow still functions. The remaining real impact is the absence of any edit/delete/deactivate control, leaving accumulating cruft and no clean removal of a mistyped active term.

findings.title: createSystemTerm performs no date validation — accepts end<start, out-of-year-range, and overlapping terms; frontend only warns
findings.evidence: createSystemTerm (:1437-1462) only checks `system_academic_year_id` and `name` are present (:1440) and that the year exists (:1441-1442); it writes start_date/end_date straight through with no start<end check, no within-year-bounds check, and no overlap check — unlike validateYearPayload for years (:809-832 which does all three). The frontend computes `overlapWith` (SACreateTerm.js:160), `outOfRange` (:161) and shows warning banners (:509-532), but `isValid` (:164-168) only blocks on missing year/order/name and `endBeforeStart`; overlap and out-of-range are non-blocking warnings. So a user can ignore the warnings and the server happily persists an invalid term.
findings.impact: Garbage term date ranges (overlapping, reversed where end==start, or outside the academic year) can be saved, which then cascade to every school on rollout and feed timetable scheduling, corrupting the calendar.
findings.suggestedFix: Add server-side validation in createSystemTerm/updateSystemTerm: reject end_date <= start_date, reject dates outside the parent year's bounds, and warn/reject on overlap with sibling terms. Return fieldErrors so the existing form error plumbing surfaces them.

verdict.reasoning: Verified in both layers. Backend createSystemTerm (superadminDataController.js:1437-1462) only validates that system_academic_year_id and name are present (:1440) and that the year exists (:1441-1442); it writes start_date/end_date straight through (:1446-1447) with no start<end, within-year-bounds, or overlap checks. This is genuinely asymmetric with academic years: validateYearPayload (:788-834) performs end<=start (:817), both-or-neither dates (:812-815), and overlap (:821-831) checks, and it IS wired into createAcademicYear (:893) and updateAcademicYear (:932). On the frontend, overlapWith (SACreateTerm.js:160) and outOfRange (:161) are rendered as non-blocking warning banners (:509-532), while isValid (:164-168) only gates on year/order/name and endBeforeStart. handleSubmit (:226) returns only on !isValid, so a super-admin can ignore the overlap/out-of-range warnings and the POST persists the invalid term. Same gap exists in updateSystemTerm (:1464-1485). Impact is real: these are global master records that cascade to every school on rollout and feed timetable scheduling. Severity medium (not high) is correct because it requires a trusted super-admin to deliberately bypass warnings or call the API directly; it is not a cross-tenant or unauthenticated exposure.
verdict.correction: One detail is mis-stated: the finding says invalid terms with "reversed where end==start" can be saved via the UI. The frontend DOES block end<=start through endBeforeStart (SACreateTerm.js:162, `new Date(endDate) <= new Date(startDate)`), so end==start and end<start are blocked client-side. The true defect is that the BACKEND has no such guard at all — a non-browser client (curl/Postman) can POST end<start, end==start, overlapping, and out-of-range dates, and the server persists them. So the overlap and out-of-range cases are bypassable through the UI (non-blocking warnings), while the reversed-date case is only reachable by hitting the API directly. The backend validation gap is the actual root cause, and it also affects updateSystemTerm, not just create.

findings.title: Rollout cascade matches per-school years/terms by case-insensitive name only — silent duplicates / wrong-row activation on any name drift
findings.evidence: The cascade joins system years/terms to per-school rows purely by LOWER(name): AcademicYear.findOrCreate keyed on `LOWER(name)=row.name` (:1092-1098) and Term.findOrCreate keyed on `LOWER(name)=st.name` (:1121-1128). There is no stable foreign key (e.g. system_academic_year_id) on pruh_core_academicyear/pruh_core_term linking back to the system record. If a school already created its own '2024/2025' year by hand, the system rollout silently adopts that row and flips it active. If a system term was renamed (e.g. SACreateTerm prefixes names as `1st Term — X`, SACreateTerm.js:231-233) after an earlier rollout, the next rollout creates a duplicate per-school term instead of updating. getRolloutPreview/getAcademicYearAdoption use the same fragile LOWER(name) match (:1184, :1328), so the 'already have it' / adoption counts drift too.
findings.impact: Cascade rollout can activate a school's pre-existing same-named (possibly differently-dated) year, or spawn duplicate terms, and the adoption/preview metrics misreport coverage. Hard-to-trace calendar drift across tenants.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a nullable `system_academic_year_id` FK to pruh_core_academicyear (and `system_term_id` to pruh_core_term), match on that in findOrCreate and in preview/adoption, and fall back to name only for legacy rows.

verdict.reasoning: Verified against actual code. rolloutAcademicYear (superadminDataController.js:1058-1168) cascade branch joins system years/terms to per-school rows purely by LOWER(name): AcademicYear.findOrCreate keyed on LOWER(name)=row.name (1092-1098) and Term.findOrCreate keyed on LOWER(name)=st.name (1121-1128). Confirmed the per-school models have NO stable FK back to the system record: AcademicYear.js (pruh_core_academicyear) columns are id/school_id/name/start_date/end_date/is_active/created_at, and Term.js (pruh_core_term) is id/school_id/academic_year_id/name/dates/is_active/created_at — neither has system_academic_year_id or system_term_id, so name is the only available join key. getRolloutPreview (1182-1184) and getAcademicYearAdoption (1321-1328) use the same LOWER(name) match. The SACreateTerm rename claim is confirmed: SACreateTerm.js:233 builds name as `${label} — ${termName.trim()}` (e.g. "1st Term — X"). Real consequences: (1) a school's hand-created same-named year is silently adopted via findOrCreate and flipped is_active=true while its other years are deactivated (1111-1117), even with different dates; (2) renaming a system term between rollouts makes the LOWER(name) match miss, so findOrCreate spawns a duplicate per-school term under the same reused schoolYear.id instead of updating; (3) preview/adoption coverage metrics drift off the same fragile match. Severity medium is appropriate: not security/guaranteed-loss, requires name collision or drift to trigger, but produces hard-to-trace cross-tenant calendar corruption and wrong-row activation when it does.
verdict.correction: Finding is accurate as stated. Minor refinements: the preview/adoption LOWER(name) queries are global (not tenant-scoped beyond grouping by school_id), and getAcademicYearAdoption's matchMap is keyed by school_id so a school with two same-named years only surfaces one — secondary effects of the same root cause. Also note the cascade's wrong-row activation deactivates ALL of that school's other academic years (lines 1111-1114), which amplifies the calendar-drift impact when the adopted row is the wrong (e.g. differently-dated) one.

findings.title: closeAcademicYear can close any year (incl. a draft) and leaves the platform with no active year, with no confirmation
findings.evidence: closeAcademicYear (:1288-1312) unconditionally sets `is_active=false`, `status='closed'` with no check that the row is currently active or that another year will take over. The UI close-out card (SARefDataManager.js:899-921) is only shown for the active year near/after its end date, but the endpoint itself has no guard, and after closing, renderHero falls back to 'No active year' (:830-837) with the platform having zero active academic year until a new rollout. There is no second-step confirm on the close-out button (:911-918) — a single click closes the live year for every school.
findings.impact: One click (or a direct API call) can drop the platform to no-active-year state, breaking any feature that resolves 'current year' for all tenants, with no undo prompt.
findings.suggestedFix: Guard closeAcademicYear to only act on the active year, require a confirm step (like the rollout modal), and either block closing until a successor is rolled out or warn explicitly that schools will be left with no active year.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified against the actual code. The two concrete sub-defects are REAL: (1) closeAcademicYear (superadminDataController.js:1288-1312) does findByPk then unconditionally sets is_active=false / status='closed' with NO check that the row is currently active — a draft or already-closed year passed by id is set to 'closed'. (2) The frontend close button (SARefDataManager.js:911-918) calls handleClose (510-518) which fires apiPost directly with NO window.confirm or modal second step. Route sa.post('/academic-years/:id/close/', superadmin.js:142) is gated only by authenticateToken + schoolScope + requireRole(['superadmin']), so a direct API call can target any id. renderHero (830-837) does fall back to 'No active year' when nothing is active. So the mechanics described are accurate.

However the IMPACT is materially overstated, which is why severity stays low (not higher): (a) NOT 'no undo' — a closed year is fully recoverable: toggleAcademicYearStatus (1016-1041) reactivates any !is_active row including a closed one (line 1023 checks is_active only, not status), and rolloutAcademicYear (1058+) also sets a year active; both demote the prior active year to 'closed' in the same transaction. (b) Zero-active is the INTENDED transient operator state, not corruption — rollout/toggle auto-close the old active year when activating the next, and the close-out card copy explicitly says closing 'frees the calendar for the next rollout.' (c) The 'breaks current-year resolution for ALL tenants' claim overstates blast radius: SystemAcademicYear is the platform master/rollout template; per-school operations resolve each school's own AcademicYear (pruh_academic_year) rows, which closing the system year does not touch. (d) The only UI-reachable close target is the active year past 90% progress / its end date (renderCloseout returns null otherwise, 899-903), so the 'close a draft' path is direct-API-only, not an accidental UI click. The action is also audited (appendSecurityAuditLog). Net: genuine but minor — a missing active-state guard plus a missing confirm dialog on a reversible, audited, superadmin-only action. Severity low is correct.
verdict.correction: The defect is real but its impact is overstated. Accurate version: closeAcademicYear lacks a guard that the target row is currently active (so a draft/closed year can be re-marked 'closed' via direct API), and the UI close button has no confirmation dialog. But it is NOT a no-undo platform-breaking action: closing is reversible (toggleAcademicYearStatus reactivates a closed year; rolloutAcademicYear re-activates one), a zero-active state is the intended transient between close and next rollout, per-school AcademicYear records are unaffected so tenant 'current year' resolution does not break platform-wide, and the only UI-exposed close target is the active year past 90%/end-date. The real, low-severity fixes are: add an is_active/status guard (or no-op if already closed) in closeAcademicYear, and add a confirm step before handleClose.

findings.title: Create-User modal offers Exam Officer / Finance Officer roles that the backend silently downgrades to School Admin
findings.evidence: SAUsers.js:53 `const ROLES_LIST = ['Super Admin', 'School Admin', 'Teacher', 'Exam Officer', 'Finance Officer'];` is fed to the role <select> (SAUsers.js:168). On submit, postUsers calls mapInviteLabelToCode(role) (superadminDataController.js:371). roleIds.js:15-25 only maps 'Super Admin'/'School Admin'/'Teacher'/'Parent'/'Principal'/'Bursar'/'Student' and `return 'schooladmin'` as the default. There is NO mapping for 'Exam Officer' or 'Finance Officer', and seedRoles.js:13-21 seeds only superadmin/teacher/student/parent/bursar/schooladmin/principal — no exam/finance role exists. So inviting an 'Exam Officer' or 'Finance Officer' creates a user with role_id of schooladmin.
findings.impact: An operator who invites an Exam Officer or Finance Officer unknowingly grants that account School Admin role_id (full tenant-admin authority), a privilege escalation versus the label shown. The two roles are also not real platform roles at all.
findings.suggestedFix: Either remove 'Exam Officer'/'Finance Officer' from ROLES_LIST until real roles exist, or add explicit mappings in mapInviteLabelToCode plus seed the corresponding roles, and make the default branch reject unknown labels (400) instead of silently falling back to schooladmin.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by reading all four cited files end to end. SAUsers.js:53 defines ROLES_LIST including 'Exam Officer' and 'Finance Officer'; line 168 renders all five as <select> options; submit (line 82) posts role:form.role to /api/users/. superadminDataController.postUsers (lines 354-381) does NO role-value validation (line 357 only checks role is truthy), then calls mapInviteLabelToCode(role) (line 371) and persists role_id (line 380). roleIds.js:15-25 has no case for 'Exam Officer'/'Finance Officer' and falls through to `return 'schooladmin'` (line 24). seedRoles.js:13-21 seeds only superadmin/teacher/student/parent/bursar/schooladmin/principal — no exam/finance role exists. So inviting either label silently creates a user with the School Admin role_id, a real privilege-escalation/data-mismatch versus the label shown, with no warning. Two accurate nuances that don't refute the defect: (1) the user is created is_active:false (line 379) so it isn't usable until activated, but the persisted role_id is genuinely schooladmin; (2) the SchoolAdmin tenant link at line 383 is keyed on the literal 'School Admin' label, so an Exam/Finance Officer gets the schooladmin role_id with no school binding — an extra integrity wrinkle. Severity high is appropriate.

findings.title: Invite User 'School' is required free-text but is silently ignored unless it exactly matches an existing school name
findings.evidence: Modal validates `if (needsSchool && !form.school.trim()) e.school = 'School is required for this role'` (SAUsers.js:68) and sends `school: form.school` as a typed string (SAUsers.js:82). Backend only links a school when `role === 'School Admin'` AND an exact name match is found: `const sch = await School.findOne({ where: { name: school } }); if (sch) await SchoolAdmin.create(...)` (superadminDataController.js:383-385). For Teacher/Exam/Finance roles the `school` value is accepted by the form but never used at all. For School Admin, a typo or near-match name finds no school and the SchoolAdmin link is silently skipped with no error returned.
findings.impact: Operator types a school, the call returns success, but the user has no school association (and for non-SA roles the field is pure theatre). The created account is orphaned and the 'School' the operator chose is lost with zero feedback.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the free-text school field with a dropdown populated from GET /api/superadmin/schools/ (send school_id, not name). In postUsers, if a school is required for the role and the id resolves to nothing, return a 400 instead of creating an unlinked user.

verdict.reasoning: Verified against the actual code. Frontend SAUsers.js makes "School" a required free-text field (line 68 validation, line 173 free-text input, line 83 sends raw string). Backend postUsers (superadminDataController.js:383-386) only links a school when role === 'School Admin' AND School.findOne({where:{name: school}}) returns an exact-name match; on no match the `if (sch)` guard is false and SchoolAdmin.create is skipped with NO error — the call still returns success (line 395-397). For Teacher/Exam Officer/Finance Officer roles the `school` value is never consumed by any linkage path (confirmed by reading the entire 354-405 function). So the finding is accurate: the operator types a school, gets "Invitation Sent", and the school is silently dropped for non-SchoolAdmin roles and for any near-miss/typo SchoolAdmin name. The endpoint is reachable (routes/superadmin.js:215). The finding is in fact UNDERSTATED: (1) mapInviteLabelToCode (roleIds.js:15-25) has no case for "Exam Officer" or "Finance Officer", so both silently fall through to the default return 'schooladmin' — inviting an exam/finance officer actually mis-creates a schooladmin-role account, a second silent data-integrity bug; (2) invited users are created is_active:false so they cannot log in until separately activated. Raising severity to high because the consequence is not merely a lost form field but silent creation of orphaned and/or wrong-role privileged accounts (a SchoolAdmin/finance/exam role with no tenant binding) returned as success, which is a data-integrity and access-control concern, not a cosmetic one.
verdict.correction: Accurate core claim, but two facts strengthen it: (a) The UI's ROLES_LIST offers "Exam Officer" and "Finance Officer", yet mapInviteLabelToCode has no mapping for those labels, so they default to roleCode 'schooladmin' — these invites create a School Admin account, not the chosen role, regardless of the school issue. (b) For ALL non-School-Admin roles the typed school is dropped with zero feedback; for School Admin a typo/near-match school name skips the SchoolAdmin link silently. In every case the API responds success:true and the user is created is_active:false (cannot log in until activated). So the impact is silent creation of orphaned or wrong-role privileged accounts, not just a lost UI field.

findings.title: Invited users are created is_active:false with no activation/credential-delivery path, yet UI claims credentials were emailed
findings.evidence: postUsers sets `is_active: false` and stores a random tempPass (superadminDataController.js:367,379) but never emails anything — there is no sendInvite/sendPasswordResetEmail call in the function (compare resetUserPassword in superadminController.js:476-479 which DOES email). The modal's success state asserts 'Credentials have been dispatched to <email>' (SAUsers.js:150) and the list toast says 'Invitation sent — user will receive credentials by email.' (SAUsers.js:553).
findings.impact: Every invited user lands inactive and never receives credentials, so they can never log in, while the SA is told the invite was emailed. The whole 'Invite User' flow produces dead accounts. getUsers also returns these as status:'inactive' with no way to activate them from this page.
findings.suggestedFix: Send an invite/credential email (or set up a first-login activation token) in postUsers, and either create the user active or add an Activate action. Do not claim 'credentials dispatched' in the UI unless an email actually went out.

verdict.reasoning: Verified against source. Backend POST /api/users/ -> data.postUsers (route bound at superadmin.js:215) creates the user with is_active:false (superadminDataController.js:379) and a random tempPass that is bcrypt-hashed into password (line 367,376) and then discarded. The function's only side effects are User.create, an optional SchoolAdmin.create, and appendSecurityAuditLog — there is NO email/invite call, and the controller does not even import utils/email or services/mailer (imports at lines 1-30). By contrast, resetUserPassword in superadminController.js:478 DOES call sendPasswordResetEmail and returns "notification email sent." Email infra exists and works (utils/email.js, services/mailer.js, used elsewhere), so the omission in postUsers is a real gap, not a missing-dependency artifact. The UI overstates the outcome on three surfaces: modal subtitle "Creates account and sends credentials via email" (SAUsers.js:135), success state "Credentials have been dispatched to <email>" (line 150), and the list toast "Invitation sent — user will receive credentials by email." (line 553). Login is hard-blocked for these accounts: authController.js:96 returns 403 "pending approval by the Superadmin" when !user.is_active && !isPortalSuper. There is no activation path for invited platform users — every other create path in this controller (students/parents/teachers/bursars/principals, lines 3039-3910) uses is_active:true, and the only is_active=true flips in the codebase (approvalController.js:166, superadminController.js:110/119/204) are gated on SCHOOL approval, not individual user invites. getUsers maps these as status:'inactive' (line 301) with no activate control on the page. Net: every invited user is a dead account, no credentials are sent, and the SA is falsely told the invite was emailed — exactly as the finding states. Severity high (not critical) is right: it breaks an operator-only admin workflow and misleads the operator, but it is not a security/data-integrity/data-loss defect.

findings.title: User list role column is derived heuristically and mislabels teachers/bursars/principals as plain 'User'
findings.evidence: mapUserToSaRow ignores the user's real role_id and infers role only from `is_superuser` / `is_staff` / presence of a SchoolAdmin link: `let role='User'; if (user.is_superuser) role='Super Admin'; else if (user.is_staff) role='Staff Admin'; else if (schoolName) role='School Admin';` (superadminDataController.js:290-293). Teachers, bursars, principals, parents and students all fall through to role='User'. getUsers only joins SchoolAdmin (superadminDataController.js:320), never Teacher/Bursar/etc.
findings.impact: The User Management role filter and role badges are wrong for most tenant users — a teacher shows as 'User', defeating the role filter (SAUsers.js:591-597) and the Governance per-role user counts which key off this same field. Operators can't reliably find users by role.
findings.suggestedFix: Join the users.role_id -> roles.code and map to the display label in mapUserToSaRow instead of guessing from is_staff/SchoolAdmin presence, so the role reflects the actual seeded role.

verdict.reasoning: Verified against the actual code. mapUserToSaRow (superadminDataController.js:288-312) derives role purely from the is_superuser/is_staff/schoolName heuristic (lines 290-293) and never reads the user's real role. getUsers (314-332) only joins SchoolAdmin (line 320), never Teacher/Bursar/Principal/Parent. Crucially, the User model (User.js:23-27, 56-58) has a NOT-NULL role_id with the `role` association eagerly loaded by defaultScope, so user.role.code and user.role.name are already present on every row returned by getUsers — the correct role was available and ignored. SA-created teachers/bursars/principals/parents/students all get real role_ids (lines 3034/3086/3283/3562/3741/3895 via requireRoleId), so the data exists. Frontend impact confirmed end-to-end: SAUsers role filter is built dynamically from emitted roles (SAUsers.js:543) and filters on u.role (line 531), so Teacher/Parent/Bursar tabs never appear; ROLE_COLORS (lines 37-46) defines Teacher/Parent colors that never render; SAGovernance.js (lines 323-327, 341) counts users by u.role keyed on each role card's apiRole, so the Teacher card (apiRole:'Teacher', line 10) and others always show 0. So the core defect — role is heuristically derived, ignores role_id, and breaks the Users filter + Governance counts — is REAL and spans two SA pages.
verdict.correction: The finding mis-states which roles get mislabeled. It claims teachers, bursars, and principals fall through to role='User'. They do NOT. The User.is_staff virtual (User.js:36-43) returns true for superadmin, schooladmin, principal, bursar, AND teacher, and the is_staff branch (line 292) is evaluated before the schoolName branch (line 293). So teachers, bursars, principals, and even schooladmins all map to 'Staff Admin' (not 'User', and schooladmins not even 'School Admin'). Only parents and students (is_staff=false, no SchoolAdmin link) actually fall through to 'User'. The net effect the finding describes — wrong role labels, a broken role filter, and wrong Governance per-role counts — is accurate; only the specific 'User' bucket attribution for teacher/bursar/principal is wrong (they collapse into 'Staff Admin' instead). Either way the real role is lost.

findings.title: Governance shows a hardcoded 'Registrar' role that does not exist in the backend
findings.backend: n/a (no role source) — real custom roles come from GET /api/sa/custom-roles/
findings.evidence: ROLE_DEFS hardcodes `{ id:'registrar', name:'Registrar', ... isCustom:true, apiRole:'Registrar' }` (SAGovernance.js:11) and it is always merged into the role list (SAGovernance.js:340). But seedRoles.js:13-21 has no registrar role and mapInviteLabelToCode has no Registrar. Its user count is `roleCounts['Registrar'] || 0` (SAGovernance.js:350 logic) so it permanently shows 0 users. Real custom roles created via the modal are stored separately in settings.custom_roles (postSaCustomRoles, superadminDataController.js:718-731).
findings.impact: Operators see a 'Registrar / Custom Role' card that is decorative — it maps to no real role, can never have users, and editing its permissions writes a settings key (`registrar`) that authorization never reads. Misleading governance surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Drop the fabricated Registrar entry from ROLE_DEFS (and the principal/teacher entries should be driven by the seeded roles list), and render only the four seeded non-superadmin roles plus genuine custom_roles from the API.

verdict.reasoning: Verified every claim against the actual code. SAGovernance.js:11 hardcodes `{ id:'registrar', name:'Registrar', ... isCustom:true, apiRole:'Registrar' }` inside ROLE_DEFS, and ROLES (line 339-342) always maps ALL of ROLE_DEFS into the rendered list, so the Registrar card always renders. Its user count is `roleCounts[r.apiRole] || 0` = `roleCounts['Registrar'] || 0` (line 341). roleCounts is built (lines 323-329) from GET /api/users/, whose `role` field — set by mapUserToSaRow (superadminDataController.js:288-293) — is ONLY ever 'User', 'Super Admin', 'Staff Admin', or 'School Admin'. It is never 'Registrar', so the card permanently shows 0 users. Backend confirms no registrar role exists: seedRoles.js seeds 7 roles (superadmin/teacher/student/parent/bursar/schooladmin/principal) with no registrar; mapInviteLabelToCode (roleIds.js:15-25) has no Registrar branch (unknown labels fall through to 'schooladmin'); a full grep for 'registrar' across the entire backend returns ZERO hits. Real custom roles created via CreateRoleModal POST /api/sa/custom-roles/ and are stored separately in settings.custom_roles by postSaCustomRoles (superadminDataController.js:718-731), then loaded into `customRoles` and merged as `extras` (line 343-352) — a code path entirely distinct from the hardcoded registrar. Editing the registrar card writes perms under key `registrar` into rbac_role_permissions via PATCH /api/admin-settings/ (line 380); a repo-wide grep shows rbac_role_permissions is referenced ONLY inside SAGovernance.js (read at 318, write at 380) and by no authorization/middleware code, so the saved permissions are dead. The finding is accurate on all points. Adjustments to severity: this is a cosmetic/data-integrity defect (a decorative role that maps to nothing and can never have users), not a security or data-loss issue, so medium is correct. One mitigating nuance the finding omits: the page already shows a prominent 'Preview — not enforced' banner (lines 437-442) stating the whole matrix does not affect authorization, which partially discloses the dead-settings-write sub-impact — but it does NOT explain that Registrar specifically is fabricated and unrealizable, so the core 'misleading governance surface' defect stands.
verdict.correction: The finding is correct. Minor clarifications: (1) The exact merge line is the `ROLE_DEFS.map(...)` at SAGovernance.js:340-342 (the cited "line 340" is right). (2) The user-count expression resolves via `roleCounts[r.apiRole] || 0` (line 341) where r.apiRole='Registrar'; mapUserToSaRow can only emit 'User'/'Super Admin'/'Staff Admin'/'School Admin', so the count is guaranteed 0 — even more strongly than stated (it also can never match the Teacher/Principal base roles). (3) The page already carries a global 'Preview — not enforced' honesty banner (lines 437-442) that discloses the matrix is non-authoritative, so the 'writes a settings key authorization never reads' sub-impact is partly acknowledged; but the registrar role itself is not flagged as fabricated, so the misleading-role defect remains real.

findings.title: 'Clone role' button on every governance role card has no handler (dead onClick)
findings.evidence: Each role card renders `<button className="sa-role-icon-btn" aria-label="Clone role"><IcCopy size={16} /></button>` with no onClick (SAGovernance.js:515). Clicking it does nothing.
findings.impact: A visible, affordance-bearing action button that silently no-ops — operators expect to clone a role to bootstrap a new one and get no response or feedback.
findings.suggestedFix: Wire the clone button to open CreateRoleModal pre-filled with the role's name+description (and copy its perms), or remove the button until clone is implemented.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at EK_SMS/src/components/superadmin/SAGovernance.js:515. The button `<button className="sa-role-icon-btn" aria-label="Clone role"><IcCopy size={16} /></button>` is rendered on every role card (inside the filteredRoles.map at line 495) and has NO onClick handler. Confirmed adversarially: (1) no `handleClone`/clone function exists anywhere in the file (grep for clone returns only this dead button); (2) the role card div at line 496 has no onClick, and a grep of all onClick/onSubmit in the file shows no parent/delegated handler that could catch the click; (3) the button is not inside a <form> (it sits in <div className="sa-role-card">), so it is not an implicit submit; (4) the same className `sa-role-icon-btn` is used twice elsewhere in the SAME file (line 91 Back button, line 121 toggle) and BOTH have onClick handlers, so this is a clear omission not an intentional decorative element; (5) the class has real CSS in SA.css:2625 including a `:hover` background/color change, so it presents as an interactive, clickable affordance. Clicking it is a silent no-op. Severity low is correct: it is a non-functional UI affordance with no data/security/tenant impact, and an alternate role-creation path exists (the 'Create' button wired to setShowCreate(true) at line 430). Note: this component also has no @media(max-width:600px) responsive rules concern in scope here — not relevant to this specific finding.

findings.title: Permission matrix is fully editable/saved but never enforced (config-only); custom-role permissions are silently discarded
findings.evidence: handleSave persists the whole perms object to settings via `ApiClient.patch('/api/admin-settings/', { settings: { rbac_role_permissions: perms } })` (SAGovernance.js:380) but nothing in the auth path reads rbac_role_permissions. The page itself admits this with the 'Preview — not enforced' banner (SAGovernance.js:437-442). Separately, CreateRoleModal POSTs `permissions: {}` (SAGovernance.js:226) and postSaCustomRoles only persists `{ id, name, description }` (superadminDataController.js:724-728) — any permissions assigned to a custom role are dropped on save.
findings.impact: The core governance promise (RBAC) is non-functional: toggling permissions changes nothing about access, and custom roles cannot carry permissions at all. The banner is honest, but this is a real workflow gap for the 'manage governance' SA responsibility.
findings.suggestedFix: Either wire rbac_role_permissions into the requireRole/authorization middleware, or scope the page to clearly 'coming soon'. Extend postSaCustomRoles to persist a permissions object and have the editor save custom-role perms under the same key.

verdict.reasoning: All three claims independently verified in the actual code. (1) SAGovernance.js:380 handleSave persists the entire perms object via ApiClient.patch('/api/admin-settings/', { settings: { rbac_role_permissions: perms } }). (2) A repo-wide grep for rbac_role_permissions returns hits ONLY inside SAGovernance.js (lines 318-319 to repopulate the editor, line 380 to save) — the key appears nowhere in backend_node. The real authorization path is middleware/requireRole.js, which matches req.user.role against a hardcoded allowedRoles array passed at route-definition time and never consults saved settings. So toggling the matrix changes nothing about access. (3) CreateRoleModal POSTs permissions:{} (SAGovernance.js:226); postSaCustomRoles (superadminDataController.js:718-736) destructures only { name, description } from req.body and stores { id, name, description } in settings.custom_roles — the permissions field is silently dropped, and the storage shape has no permissions slot at all. Medium severity is correct: the page carries an honest 'Preview — not enforced' banner (lines 436-442), so this is an incomplete-feature/workflow gap for the SA 'manage governance' responsibility rather than a silent security hole.
verdict.correction: Finding is accurate as written. One refinement to add: the honesty banner (lines 436-442) covers ONLY the permission matrix; it does not disclose the custom-role permissions drop. verdict.reasoning: Verified independently against all cited code. (1) Route: backend_node/src/routes/superadmin.js:211 `sa.get('/grade-stats/', data.getGradeStats)` is exactly the endpoint SABenchmarks.js:192 calls. Adjusting severity from high to medium: the page degrades gracefully (renders '—' and an empty-state message, no crash and no fabricated numbers), and it is purely a missing backend aggregation on an analytics surface — real and visible (two of four headline academic-quality outputs permanently dead on the USP Benchmarks page) but not a crash, data-integrity, or security defect, so 'high' is slightly overstated.

findings.title: Top-Schools 'Perf. Index' is a relative student-count ratio mislabeled as a performance/integrity metric
findings.evidence: SABenchmarks.js:234 computes `perf: parseFloat((s.student_count / Math.max(1, schoolStats[0]?.student_count || 1) * 10).toFixed(1))`. The card header (315) calls the table 'Ranked by Integrity & Performance Index' and the column (325) is 'Perf. Index', but the value is purely a normalized headcount ratio — nothing to do with grades, integrity, or academic performance. With getSchoolStats returning 0 students for all schools, every perf value is also 0/NaN.
findings.impact: The Super Admin reads 'Performance Index' / 'Integrity' as an academic-quality ranking; it is actually 'this school has X% as many students as the biggest school'. Combined with the zero-count bug, the column is both mislabeled and empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Either rank by a real academic metric (avg_total / pass rate from grade data, which getGradeStats.per_school could surface), or relabel the column 'Relative Size' and drop the 'Integrity & Performance' header wording.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified against source. SABenchmarks.js:234 computes `perf: parseFloat((s.student_count / Math.max(1, schoolStats[0]?.student_count || 1) * 10).toFixed(1))` — purely the school's headcount as a fraction of the largest school's headcount, scaled to 10 (the biggest school always = 10.0). It has nothing to do with grades, integrity, or academic performance. The card subtitle at :315 reads "Ranked by Integrity & Performance Index" and the column header at :325 is "Perf. Index", so a value that is just a relative student-count ratio is presented to the Super Admin as a performance/integrity ranking. That is a genuine data-mismatch / mislabel.

Backend confirms the zero-count claim: getSchoolStats in superadminDataController.js (the only handler for the /api/school-stats/ route, superadmin.js:212) hardcodes `student_count: 0` for every school (lines 413-420). With all counts 0, perf evaluates to parseFloat((0/1*10).toFixed(1)) = 0 for every school — uniformly 0.

Two corrections to the original wording: (1) the value is always 0, never NaN — the `|| 1` and `Math.max(1, ...)` guards make a NaN impossible, so the finding's "0/NaN" is slightly wrong. (2) In practice the perf column never even renders: the backend response omits `is_approved` (and `school_name`), so the frontend filter `data.stats.filter(s => s.is_approved)` at :197 always yields an empty array, topSchools is empty, and the table shows the "No approved schools on the platform yet." empty state (:320) instead of any rows. So the column is mislabeled AND, separately, unreachable rather than merely "empty".

Severity lowered to low: this is a read-only monitoring page; the defect is a cosmetic/semantic mislabel of a derived metric (plus an upstream stub-data bug), with no security, persistence, or functional-correctness impact. The mislabel is real, but medium overstates a label/derivation mismatch on a card that currently renders no rows at all.
verdict.correction: The perf value is uniformly 0, not "0/NaN" — the `|| 1` and `Math.max(1, ...)` guards prevent any NaN. More significantly, the "Perf. Index" column is not actually reached in practice: getSchoolStats returns rows without an `is_approved` field, so the frontend's `.filter(s => s.is_approved)` (SABenchmarks.js:197) produces an empty array, topSchools is empty, and the table renders the "No approved schools on the platform yet." empty state (:320) rather than any perf values. The accurate statement: line 234's `perf` is a relative student-headcount ratio (each school's student_count / the largest school's student_count * 10) mislabeled as a "Perf. Index" / "Integrity & Performance Index" (lines 315, 325) — a real semantic data-mismatch — but it is a label/derivation defect on a read-only page whose rows currently don't render at all, so severity is low rather than medium.
