(3) SAAnalytics.js:301 SchoolCard kebab `<button className="san-dots-btn" onClick={e => e.stopPropagation()} aria-label="Options">` only stops propagation and opens no menu; grep for menu/dropdown state in the file returns nothing, so it is purely decorative. These are genuine dead-end UI controls. Severity correctly stays low: cosmetic only, no data/security/crash impact, and working alternate navigation exists (the card body navigates via onView, the analytics table has a working View button). Line numbers in the evidence all match exactly.

findings.title: Newly added countries/regions/cities are created is_active=false and never appear in registration dropdowns
findings.evidence: All three models default is_active to false: Country.js:7, Region.js:8, City.js:9 (`is_active: { type: DataTypes.BOOLEAN, defaultValue: false }`). The create handlers never set is_active: createCountry (superadminDataController.js:1943 `Country.create({ name })`), createRegion (:2023), createCity (:2115) all omit is_active, so every new row is INACTIVE. The downstream consumer filters on active: Register.js:1391 `(r.countries||[]).filter(c => c.is_active)`, :1415 `(res.regions||[]).filter(r => r.is_active)`, :1440 `(res.cities||[]).filter(c => c.is_active)`. Net effect: a Super Admin adds 'Sierra Leone' here, it saves 'successfully', shows status 'Inactive' in the table, and silently does NOT appear in the school registration geography dropdowns until the SA separately clicks the toggle on each row.
findings.impact: The stated purpose of this page ('Used to populate geography dropdowns during registration', SuperadminDashboard.js:1325) is broken on the happy path. Operators add geography and it never reaches registrants; the failure is silent (no error, no hint).
findings.suggestedFix: Set is_active: true on create in createCountry/createRegion/createCity (or change the model default to true), so added geography is live by default. Alternatively keep default-off but surface it in the UI ('Inactive rows are hidden from registration — activate to publish').

verdict.reasoning: Verified end-to-end in the actual code. (1) All three models default is_active to false: Country.js:7, Region.js:8, City.js:9 each `is_active: { type: DataTypes.BOOLEAN, defaultValue: false }`. (2) The create handlers never set is_active: createCountry (superadminDataController.js:1943 `Country.create({ name: ... })`), createRegion (:2023 `Region.create({ country_id, name })`), createCity (:2115 `City.create({ country_id, region_id, name })`) — so every new row is INACTIVE. Routes confirm POST /api/countries|regions|cities -> these handlers (superadmin.js:172/178/182). (3) The SA create UI (SARefDataManager.doSave, L407-416) only POSTs the configured fields (name + country_id/region_id); there is no is_active field in the geography configs (SuperadminDashboard.js:1329-1331/1342-1345/1356-1360) and no active-on-create. (4) The table renders the fresh row as literally "Inactive" (SARefDataManager.js:1321) with a manual toggle button (L1384-1394) the SA must click. (5) The registration consumer filters active-only: Register.js:1391 countries `.filter(c => c.is_active)`, :1415 regions `.filter(r => r.is_active)`, :1440 cities `.filter(c => c.is_active)`. Net effect matches the finding: a Super Admin adds 'Sierra Leone', it saves 'successfully', shows 'Inactive', and is filtered out of registration dropdowns until separately toggled. Adversarial nuances that adjust (not refute) the finding: (a) For COUNTRIES there is NO fallback at all, so a new country is genuinely, silently absent from the registration country dropdown — the finding is fully literal here, and this is the cascade entry point. (b) For REGIONS/CITIES Register.js falls back to the public geo API by country name (fetchStates L1418 / fetchCities L1443), but ONLY when the curated active list is empty (`names.length === 0`); so a new inactive region added to a country that already has active curated regions is still silently hidden, while a brand-new country's regions/cities degrade to the public API rather than going blank. So the defect holds in all three cases, with regions/cities partly mitigated against a totally-empty dropdown. Severity lowered high->medium: no data loss (the row is saved), the SA gets an explicit visible "Inactive" badge and a one-click toggle in the same row, and regions/cities degrade gracefully via the public geo API. It is a poor/confusing default + missing affordance (no active-on-create and no hint that inactive rows are excluded from registration), not a hard breakage. Real, worth fixing — likely set is_active:true on create (or add an active checkbox + a "hidden from registration" hint on inactive rows).
verdict.correction: Finding is accurate. One refinement to the impact: "silently does NOT appear ... never reaches registrants" is literally true for COUNTRIES (no fallback path), but for REGIONS and CITIES Register.js falls back to the public geo API (fetchStates/fetchCities) when the curated active list is empty, so a brand-new country's regions/cities still populate from the public API rather than rendering blank. A newly added inactive region/city for a country that already has other active curated regions is still hidden (fallback won't trigger because the list isn't empty). The new curated row is hidden from registration until the SA toggles it in all three cases.

findings.title: Deleting a country/region hard-deletes the row and orphans all child regions/cities with no FK guard or force flow
findings.evidence: deleteCountry (superadminDataController.js:1967-1978) and deleteRegion (:2052-2063) do an unconditional hard `await row.destroy()` with no check for dependent rows. Region.js / City.js declare country_id/region_id as plain BIGINT columns with NO Sequelize associations or DB-level cascade, so deleting a country leaves its regions and cities pointing at a non-existent country_id (same for region->cities). The frontend handleDelete (SARefDataManager.js:472) even supports a `?force=1` + 409 `requiresForce` confirm flow, but the geography controllers never emit 409/requiresForce, so the user gets no 'this country has N regions/cities' warning — one click silently orphans the whole subtree.
findings.impact: Data integrity loss: orphaned regions/cities remain in pruh_system_region/pruh_system_city referencing deleted parents; cities can outlive their region/country. The cities cascade in the form (region filtered by country_id) then shows regions whose country no longer exists, or cities under a deleted region.
findings.suggestedFix: Before destroy, count children (Region.count({where:{country_id:id}}), City.count({where:{region_id:id}} / {country_id:id}}); if >0 return 409 with requiresForce + the count (matching the shell's existing force flow), and on force either block, cascade-delete, or deactivate. At minimum block deletion of a country/region that still has children.

verdict.reasoning: Verified against all cited code. deleteCountry (superadminDataController.js:1967-1978) and deleteRegion (2052-2063) — plus deleteCity (2151-2162) — each do an unconditional hard `await row.destroy()` with no dependent-row check and never emit a 409/requiresForce. Region.js and City.js declare country_id/region_id as plain `BIGINT NOT NULL` with NO Sequelize `references`/FK; associations.js has ZERO Country/Region/City associations (grep returned no matches), so Sequelize imposes no cascade or guard. I also went one level deeper than the prior auditor and checked the DB DDL (migrations/2026-05-18-all-new-tables.sql:519-549): pruh_system_region/pruh_system_city use plain BIGINT columns with only a non-FK INDEX (no FOREIGN KEY / REFERENCES / ON DELETE), so MySQL itself will not reject the delete either — confirming the orphan is truly silent, not blocked by the DB. The frontend handleDelete (SARefDataManager.js:467-485) genuinely supports the `?force=1` + 409 `requiresForce` confirm flow, and that exact pattern IS implemented elsewhere in the SAME controller for academic-year delete (term_count guard at lines 986-990, and a parallel date-change force guard at 944-948), proving the safety pattern exists but was never wired into the geography controllers. Net effect: deleting a country/region leaves child regions/cities pointing at a non-existent parent; getRegions/getCities filter only by country_id/region_id without validating parent existence, so the registration cascade dropdowns can surface orphaned rows. The defect is real and accurately described. I downgraded severity high->medium: this is operator-only (super-admin) reference/master geography data, low-churn, not transactional PII, and the failure mode is dropdown inconsistency rather than corruption of tenant/financial/grade data — so the blast radius doesn't meet the bar for high. Title/category/evidence are otherwise correct, no correction needed beyond severity.

findings.title: Geography table shows raw 'Inactive' status with no indication that inactive = hidden from registration
findings.evidence: In non-hero mode the status cell renders just `item.is_active ? 'Active' : 'Inactive'` (SARefDataManager.js:1321) and the toggle title is the bare 'Activate'/'Deactivate' (:1387). Nothing on the page explains that an inactive country/region/city is excluded from the registration dropdowns (the actual behaviour per Register.js:1391/1415/1440). Combined with the default-inactive bug above, an operator sees a freshly added, correctly-named row marked 'Inactive' and has no signal that it is therefore invisible to registrants.
findings.impact: Operators cannot tell why their newly added geography doesn't show up downstream; the active/inactive toggle reads as a cosmetic flag rather than a publish switch.
findings.suggestedFix: Relabel the toggle/status to convey publishing (e.g. 'Live'/'Hidden' or 'Published'/'Unpublished'), and add a subtitle/tooltip: 'Only active entries appear in the school registration dropdowns.'

verdict.correction: Confirmed but partially overstated. The cited code is accurate: in non-hero mode the status cell renders the bare label `item.is_active ? 'Active' : 'Inactive'` (SARefDataManager.js:1321) and the toggle button title is the bare 'Activate'/'Deactivate' (line 1387). There is no per-field hint, legend, or tooltip on the status column/toggle explaining that inactive geography is excluded from registration dropdowns. The downstream behaviour is real: Register.js filters geography by is_active before populating the dropdowns (countries 1391, regions 1415, cities 1440), so an inactive country/region/city is genuinely invisible to registrants. The toggle therefore is a de-facto publish switch with no UI signal saying so.\n\nWhat the finding misses: the COUNTRIES page subtitle already states 'Countries where schools can be located. Used to populate geography dropdowns during registration.' (SuperadminDashboard.js:1325), so the Countries operator does get a partial signal that this data feeds registration (though still not that the toggle is the publish switch). The REGIONS subtitle (1338) and CITIES subtitle (1352) say nothing about registration at all, so the gap is real and strongest for those two pages. This is a UX-clarity shortfall, not a functional or security defect — no data loss, the toggle works, and one of three pages carries a partial hint. The evidence also leans on a separate 'default-inactive bug above' which I could not and did not verify here; the vague-UI claim stands on its own without it.
verdict.reasoning: I opened SARefDataManager.js and confirmed the exact lines cited (status cell 1318-1322, toggle 1384-1394), opened Register.js and confirmed is_active filtering of the geography dropdowns (1391/1415/1440), and read all three geography invocations in SuperadminDashboard.js (1322-1362) plus the field defs. The defect is genuinely present: nothing on the regions/cities pages, and nothing on the toggle/status control of any page, explains that inactive = hidden from registration. I downgraded medium to low because it is purely an explanatory/cosmetic clarity issue (no functional break, no data/security impact) and the Countries page already carries a partial registration hint, so the finding is real but slightly overstated.

findings.title: getRegions/getCities resolve parent names with per-row findByPk (N+1 queries)
findings.evidence: getRegions (superadminDataController.js:2002-2009) maps each region through `await Country.findByPk(r.country_id)` inside Promise.all — one extra SELECT per region. getCities (:2087-2098) is worse: per city it issues `Country.findByPk` AND `Region.findByPk` (two extra SELECTs per row). With no association/include and no caching, listing M cities fires ~2M+1 queries.
findings.impact: Slow list loads as geography grows; unnecessary DB load on every dropdown fetch (these GETs are also public/unauthenticated, so externally hittable).
findings.suggestedFix: Define Sequelize associations (Region.belongsTo(Country), City.belongsTo(Country)/belongsTo(Region)) and use a single findAll with include, or fetch all parent names in one bulk query keyed by id and map in memory.

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly against the cited code. getRegions (superadminDataController.js:2001-2009) calls `await Country.findByPk(r.country_id)` once per region inside Promise.all — N+1 SELECTs. getCities (2086-2098) is worse: per city it issues BOTH `Country.findByPk` AND `Region.findByPk`, i.e. ~2N+1 SELECTs. Both use `Region.findAll`/`City.findAll` with no `include` and no caching. I confirmed the "no association" claim independently: grep for Country|Region|City in models/associations.js returns ZERO matches, so no belongsTo/include exists — the parent-name resolution genuinely relies on per-row findByPk. I also confirmed the "public/unauthenticated" claim: routes/superadmin.js:90-91 register GET /regions and GET /cities BEFORE `router.use(authenticateToken)` at line 95, under an explicit "Public reference data endpoints (no auth required)" comment, so they are externally hittable without a token. The finding is accurate as stated. Severity "low" is correct, not higher: this is bounded master/reference data (countries->regions->cities) normally fetched with a `?country_id=` filter by the registration dropdown cascade, so per-request cardinality is small; findAll has no LIMIT but real result sets are modest. It's a genuine, easily-fixed efficiency defect (add belongsTo associations + include, or batch-load parents into a Map) but not a correctness bug or a meaningful availability risk at expected scale.

findings.title: Global platform settings (/admin-settings/) are writable by ANY authenticated user — not super-admin gated
findings.evidence: routes/superadmin.js:107-108 mounts `router.get('/admin-settings/', data.getAdminSettings)` and `router.patch('/admin-settings/', data.patchAdminSettings)` on the BASE router, BEFORE the superadmin sub-router `const sa = express.Router(); sa.use(requireRole(['superadmin']))` at line 111-112. The base router only has `router.use(authenticateToken); router.use(schoolScope)` (lines 95-96), and schoolScope.js never blocks any role (it only sets req.schoolId). patchAdminSettings (superadminDataController.js:270-285) has no internal role check — it blindly does `merged = { ...parsed, ...incoming }; row.settings_json = JSON.stringify(merged)` on the single global row (id:1, loadSettings:111-123). So a teacher/parent/student/school-admin token can read AND overwrite platform_name, maintenance_mode, allow_registrations, branding_logo/favicon URLs, security flags, audit retention, etc.
findings.impact: Any logged-in user of any tenant can flip the whole platform into maintenance mode, close registrations, change platform branding URLs, or read the super admin's stored phone/bio — a cross-tenant privilege escalation and integrity hole.
findings.suggestedFix: Move the /admin-settings/ GET+PATCH routes onto the `sa` router (after requireRole(['superadmin'])), or add an explicit `if (req.user.role !== 'superadmin') return res.status(403)` guard inside getAdminSettings/patchAdminSettings. Keep /profile/ and /change-password/ shared (they operate on req.user.id) but gate the global settings row.

findings.title: Security tab toggles (Global 2FA Enforcement, Auto Grade Locking, Session Timeout) persist but are never enforced
findings.evidence: SASettings.js:741-784 renders 'Global 2FA Enforcement' (twoFA), 'Auto Grade Locking' (autoLock) and 'Session Timeout' slider, and saveSecuritySettings (lines 639-654) PATCHes them into admin-settings JSON. But these are only stored as flags — nothing in the backend reads settings.twoFA / settings.autoLock / settings.sessionTimeout to actually enforce 2FA, lock grades after 24h, or expire sessions. The toggles present as live security controls (no honesty banner, unlike the Lockdown/Backup cards which DO disclose 'not enforced').
findings.impact: An operator believes they have enforced global 2FA / auto grade-locking / a session timeout, but logins, grades, and sessions are completely unaffected. False sense of security on the platform's headline (grade-integrity) controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Either wire these flags into the auth/grade/session middleware so they take effect, or add an explicit 'Recorded — enforcement pending' disclosure on the Security Configuration card the same way LockdownActive (line 477-479) and the Backups tab (line 1155-1158) already do.

findings.title: Bulk Export offers PDF format + Grades/Audit/Users datasets that the backend silently ignores
findings.evidence: SASettings.js:962-989 offers four dataset checkboxes (schools/grades/audit/users) and three formats (CSV/JSON/PDF), and the request sends `datasets=...&format=pdf` (lines 1215-1219). But getSaExport (superadminDataController.js:738-776) IGNORES req.query.datasets entirely and ALWAYS queries only School rows; for format it handles only 'json', and anything else (including 'pdf') falls through to the CSV branch (lines 764-771) returning `Content-Type: text/csv` + filename `eksms_export.csv`. So selecting Grades/Audit/Users still exports the schools list, and selecting PDF downloads a CSV.
findings.impact: An operator exporting 'Audit Logs as PDF' for a compliance request actually receives the schools master list as a CSV — wrong data, wrong format, no error. Compliance/audit workflow is broken and misleading despite the partial in-modal callout.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement per-dataset export (grades/audit/users) and a real PDF path in getSaExport, OR disable the unimplemented dataset checkboxes and the PDF format button in the UI until backed. The honesty note at line 1205 should not substitute for not shipping non-functional options.

findings.title: Super-admin profile prefs (phone, bio, avatarColor, language, timezone) are saved into the single shared global settings row
findings.evidence: SAProfile.js:205 saves `{ phone, bio, language, timezone, avatarColor }` via `ApiClient.patch('/api/admin-settings/', { settings: {...} })`, and reads them back from the same endpoint on mount (lines 147-156). admin-settings is the ONE global row id:1 (loadSettings:111-123) shared with platform-wide config. getProfile (superadminDataController.js:192-208) returns only full_name/email/username/date_joined and never phone/bio. Combined with the un-gated route above, any authenticated user can read the super admin's phone/bio out of /admin-settings/.
findings.impact: Personal profile fields live in platform config rather than on the user record; works only because there's exactly one super admin, and leaks PII given the missing role gate. A second platform operator would overwrite the first's phone/bio.
findings.suggestedFix: Persist phone/bio/avatarColor/language/timezone on the User record (or a per-user profile table) via /profile/, not the global admin-settings JSON; return them from getProfile.

findings.title: Profile photo (avatarSrc) is only stored in localStorage — lost on any other browser/device
findings.evidence: SAProfile.js:194-205 handleSave writes the base64 avatar only to `localStorage.setItem(profileKey, ...)` (profileKey = `ek-sms-profile-${user.id}`, line 105) and to the in-memory parent via onAvatarChange; the server PATCH at line 205 deliberately sends only avatarColor, NOT avatarSrc. There is no /sa/branding/-style endpoint for the user's own avatar. The 'Upload Photo' button (line 324) and camera button therefore produce a photo that exists only on the current machine. (Note: the per-user key correctly prevents cross-account leak, and the old shared key is cleared in SuperadminDashboard.js:615 — that part is fine.)
findings.impact: Operator uploads a profile photo, sees it persist, then logs in from another device or after clearing storage and the photo is gone with no warning. Zero server persistence.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a real avatar upload endpoint (reuse the multipart branding pattern in routes/superadmin.js:31-40/126) storing the file under /uploads and saving the URL on the user; or clearly label the avatar as device-local.

findings.title: 'Manage 2FA' enrollment is an entirely non-functional preview (QR, OTP, recovery codes all illustrative)
findings.evidence: TwoFAView (SASettings.js:316-461): the QR is a hardcoded decorative SVG (lines 372-384), the OTP boxes are never validated, totpKey/recoveryCodes default to empty (lines 17-18) so the 'Manual Entry Key' renders blank and the recovery grid is empty, and onComplete (line 692) just toasts '2FA enrollment is a preview — nothing was changed'. The Save/Copy recovery-code buttons (lines 428-433) have no onClick. To its credit there is a clear honesty banner (lines 360-366).
findings.impact: The headline 'Manage 2FA' account-security action does nothing. Acceptable only because it is honestly labelled, but it is a dead-end screen reachable from a primary settings button.
findings.suggestedFix: Either implement TOTP enrollment/verification end to end, or replace the elaborate fake wizard with a single 'Two-factor authentication — coming soon' state to avoid a multi-step dead-end.

findings.title: 'Record Backup Entry' writes a timestamp + fabricated filename/size but produces no actual backup
findings.evidence: postSaBackupManual (superadminDataController.js:673-705) fabricates `backupFilename = eksms-backup-<ts>.sql` and a hardcoded `estimatedSizeBytes = 2048000` ('~2MB estimated'), stores them in settings.last_backup_meta, and returns them as if real (lines 696-700). No DB dump is created. The UI is honest about this (lines 1155-1158 and toast 'no database dump is produced yet'), and the button label was renamed to 'Record Backup Entry'.
findings.impact: Low because it is disclosed, but the response still presents a concrete filename and size that imply a real artifact exists; an operator could mistake the entry for a recoverable backup.
findings.suggestedFix: Don't emit a fake .sql filename and fixed 2MB size for a backup that doesn't exist — either run mysqldump and report the true file/size, or store only the timestamp + an explicit 'no artifact' marker.

findings.title: Emergency Lockdown records state + audit log only; enforcement is unimplemented (returns sessions_terminated:0)
findings.evidence: postSaLockdown (superadminDataController.js:641-671) writes lockdown_state into the settings JSON and appends an audit entry, then returns `affected: { sessions_terminated: 0, grades_locked: 0 }` (line 665) — nothing blocks logins, kills sessions, or locks grades regardless of the chosen protocol (grade-lock/login-suspend/full-blackout). The UI is consistently honest about this (LockdownActive lines 477-505, confirm modal lines 1276-1278, status pill 'Recorded (not enforced)').
findings.impact: Low/disclosed: the operator can log a lockdown for audit but it has no protective effect; the three distinct 'Protocol' radio options are cosmetic since all behave identically.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement at least login-suspension enforcement keyed off lockdown_state in the auth middleware, or collapse the three identical-behaviour protocol options until enforcement exists.

findings.title: Server-side change-password accepts any non-empty new password (no length/strength check)
findings.evidence: postChangePassword (superadminDataController.js:233-257) only checks both fields present and that current_password matches via bcrypt.compare; it then hashes whatever new_password is given with no minimum length/complexity validation and no 'must differ from current' check. The client enforces strength (calcStrength + strengthLvl>=3 in SASettings PasswordView and SAProfile), but a direct API call could set a 1-char password.
findings.impact: Client-only password policy; the documented platform security posture (12+ chars, complexity) is bypassable via the API.
findings.suggestedFix: Mirror the client policy server-side in postChangePassword (reject new_password shorter than 12 / failing complexity) and reject new === current.

findings.title: Branding logo/favicon upload persists a URL but is never applied to the running app
findings.evidence: postSaBranding (superadminDataController.js:608-628) saves the uploaded file under /uploads/branding and stores its URL in settings.branding_logo/branding_favicon — this part is real (multer wired at routes/superadmin.js:126). But nothing consumes branding_logo.url to actually render the platform logo or swap the document favicon; the SuperadminDashboard shell and index.html don't read it. The General-tab Branding boxes (SASettings.js:1076-1097) only echo the preview back.
findings.impact: Operator uploads a system logo/favicon and it appears to save, but the console/app branding never changes — a half-wired feature with no visible result anywhere.
findings.suggestedFix: Consume settings.branding_logo.url in the dashboard header/login and inject branding_favicon into the document <link rel=icon>, or label the upload as 'stored for future use'.

findings.title: SAVersionCompare page is dead code — no UI path navigates to it
findings.evidence: SuperadminDashboard.js:1153-1158 renders SAAppHistory with an onCompare prop: `<SAAppHistory school={...} onBack={...} onCompare={() => handleCompare(selectedSchool)} />`. But SAAppHistory.js:24 declares `export default function SAAppHistory({ school, onBack })` — it never destructures or calls onCompare, and its JSX (lines 48-131) has no Compare button. handleCompare (SuperadminDashboard.js:564-567) sets activePage='version-compare', and the page is registered (line 367, rendered at 1161-1168), but nothing else triggers it. So SAVersionCompare is completely unreachable from the running app.
findings.impact: An entire built page (SAVersionCompare) can never be opened by the operator. The wiring looks complete but the trigger button was removed from SAAppHistory, leaving orphaned code and a confusing half-wired feature.
findings.suggestedFix: Either drop SAVersionCompare + handleCompare + the version-compare route entirely (it is honestly just a single-submission read-only view that duplicates SAReview), or add a real 'Review submission' button inside SAAppHistory that destructures and calls onCompare.

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly in the code. SAAppHistory.js:24 declares `export default function SAAppHistory({ school, onBack })` — it does NOT destructure `onCompare`, and its JSX (lines 48-131) contains no Compare/Compare-Versions button (the comment at lines 18-23 explicitly notes the old "Compare Versions" diff was removed). SuperadminDashboard.js:1153-1158 still passes `onCompare={() => handleCompare(selectedSchool)}` into SAAppHistory, but since the prop is never read or called, that wiring is inert. `handleCompare` (SuperadminDashboard.js:564-567) is the ONLY setter of `activePage='version-compare'`, and a codebase-wide grep shows `handleCompare` is referenced in exactly one place: that unused `onCompare` prop (line 1157). Every other occurrence of `version-compare` is passive array membership (page-title logic L272, registered-pages list L367, sub-tab/breadcrumb filters L625/676/1573) or the render branch L1161-1168 — none is a clickable nav item or button. permissions.js:35 only grants access if the page is reached; it is not a trigger. Therefore SAVersionCompare (a complete, real page: it renders the submission fields and a live Approve CTA at L63-73, not a placeholder) is genuinely unreachable from the running app. Finding confirmed and accurately stated.
verdict.correction: Finding is accurate as written. Only adjustment is severity: this is orphaned/dead-nav code with no functional, data, or security impact. SAReview already provides the full approve/reject/request-changes workflow, and SAVersionCompare itself is just a read-only single-submission view (it openly states EK-SMS stores no prior revisions to diff). The operator loses nothing reachable; this is a code-cleanliness defect, so severity is low rather than medium. Fix is either to delete SAVersionCompare + handleCompare + the version-compare route/array entries, or to add a Compare/Review button in SAAppHistory that destructures and calls onCompare.

findings.title: approval_date is fabricated as registration_date in the serializer
findings.evidence: superadminController.js:35 `const regDate = p.created_at ? new Date(p.created_at).toISOString() : null;` then line 66 `approval_date: approved ? regDate : null`. There is no real approved-at column; approval_date is just the registration date for any approved school. SAApplications.js:79-88 computes avgReview as the mean of `(new Date(s.approval_date) - new Date(s.registration_date))` — which is always exactly 0 because the two values are identical, so 'Avg Review' always renders '0m' (or '—'). SAReview.js:373-377 also shows an 'Approved' date that is really the registration date.
findings.impact: The 'Avg Review' KPI on the Onboarding page is meaningless (always 0m), and the 'Approved' date shown on the review screen is wrong (it shows when the school registered, not when it was approved). Operator sees fabricated review-time metrics.

verdict.reasoning: The finding's PRIMARY claim is refuted by the code.
